weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_attribu.ux: aws s3api get-object-attributes returns the same fields as on AWS.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_attribu.what: GetObjectAttributesHandler parses x-amz-object-attributes (only ETag, Checksum, StorageClass, ObjectSize, ObjectParts are valid), x-amz-max-parts (capped at 1000) and x-amz-part-number-marker. It resolves the entry by version, preferring .versions when present, then the null object, and sets x-amz-version-id. A delete marker answers NoSuchKey with x-amz-delete-marker. It re-runs the policy for the (version) attributes action and, for a versionId, the version read grant, and evaluates conditional headers against the resolved entry. The response includes only the requested attributes. ObjectParts comes from the stored multipart part boundaries (buildObjectAttributesParts), with sizes from offsets or summed chunks.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_attribu.why: Consequence: SDKs use this to verify multipart uploads and checksums without downloading; wrong part sizes or checksums make integrity checks fail. Design: the handler reads only metadata, and part sizes come from boundaries recorded at completion. AWS compatibility: AWS requires both s3:GetObjectVersionAttributes and the version read grant for a versioned request; that is enforced here.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy.go.character: CopyObject and UploadPartCopy: source resolution and authorization, metadata/tag directives, the metadata-only self-copy, chunk-level copying between volume servers (plain, ranged, SSE-C, SSE-KMS, cross-encryption, inline), and committing the destination under every versioning state
gotchas: Request encryption headers are validated before the destination bucket's default is added as headers, and the default is added only after the ACL re-authentication; moving it earlier makes the re-auth see headers the client never signed, moving the validation later lets a malformed request through.
With REPLACE, a repeated x-amz-meta-* header keeps only its last value, while CreateMultipartUpload (ParseS3Metadata) joins repeats with ','.
copyChunks and copyChunksForRange return on the first failed chunk while the other workers keep copying.
UploadPartCopy writes the part with mkFile on the default filer, not the key's owner filer.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy.go.if_broken: Copies read sources the caller may not read, produce unreadable encrypted objects, leave two entries sharing chunks, or lose versions.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy.go.issue_note: Copied data is not cleaned up when the copy fails after the chunks were written. CopyObject copies every chunk to new needles (executeUnifiedCopyStrategy) and only then runs finalizeCopyDestination under the object write lock, which re-checks the destination conditions (If-Match / If-None-Match). Neither a 412 there nor a filer write error deletes dstEntry.Chunks; the same holds when UploadPartCopy's mkFile of the part fails after copyChunksForRange. PutObject handles the equivalent failures with deleteOrphanedChunks (s3api_object_handlers_put.go); copy has no such call, so each failed copy leaks the full copied size in volume servers until volume.fsck. The cleanup must skip the key-rotation case that hands back the source's own chunks. Separately, UploadPartCopy resolves the source without prefixObjectSource (CopyObject applies it), so copying a part from a key that also has nested keys under it is answered NoSuchKey. Reproduced at b9866bae: a CopyObject whose filer write fails answers 500 and leaves the copied chunk on the volume server with no delete issued; classifyCopySourceError answers NoSuchKey for a prefix object on the UploadPartCopy path and passes on the CopyObject path. The destination conditions are checked before the copy and again under the lock, so the 412 leak needs a destination written in between.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy.go.ux: aws s3 cp/mv between keys and buckets, metadata edits via copy-in-place, version restores, and multipart copies of objects larger than 5 GiB work as on AWS.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy.go.what: CopyObjectHandler parses X-Amz-Copy-Source (bucket, key, versionId) and runs the checks in order: table-bucket path, source/destination names, request encryption headers (before bucket defaults are added), directives, storage class, s3:GetObject on the source (authorizeCopySource, then the tag-aware policy recheck), destination ACL, the destination bucket's default encryption added as headers (after the ACL check, because that check re-authenticates the request and these headers are not in its SignedHeaders, #12436), source resolution by versioning state (prefix objects flattened, remote-only sources cached), and source conditions (x-amz-copy-source-if-*) plus destination conditions. A self-copy that only changes metadata, tags or storage class and needs no re-encryption updates the entry in place (routed to the key's owner filer with snapshot retries, or under the object write lock). Otherwise it builds a destination entry. Ownership, ACL and lock keys are not copied, and conflicting SSE keys are filtered (shouldSkipEncryptionHeader). processMetadataBytes applies COPY/REPLACE, the destination lock headers or bucket default are applied, and data is produced either inline (processInlineContentForCopy) or by executeUnifiedCopyStrategy. finalizeCopyDestination then commits a new version (with rollback if the latest-pointer flip fails), a null version, or a plain object on the owner filer. CopyObjectPartHandler validates partNumber/uploadId and copy-source-range, takes the re-encryption slow path when SSE, checksums or inline content require it, and otherwise copies the overlapping chunks (copyChunksForRange, which also computes the part MD5) into the part entry. The rest of the file is the per-chunk machinery: assign (with the destination bucket's collection passed explicitly, as PutObject does, so with a filer group a copy and a put of one bucket land in the same collection, #12499), download or stream, decrypt/re-encrypt with per-chunk SSE metadata, and upload.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy.go.when: PUT /<bucket>/<key> with X-Amz-Copy-Source (CopyObject) and PUT ?partNumber&uploadId with X-Amz-Copy-Source (UploadPartCopy).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy.go.why: Consequence: server-side copy is how clients rename, restore old versions, change storage class or encryption, and assemble large objects (UploadPartCopy); a mistake corrupts data or bypasses source authorization. Design: copy duplicates chunks rather than sharing them, because nothing refcounts needles, so two entries on one chunk list would lose data when either is deleted. Only an in-place rewrite of the same unversioned entry may reuse the source chunks (copyReplacesSourceEntry). The source is authorized separately because the route's auth only covers the destination URL. AWS compatibility: COPY/REPLACE semantics, binary/octet-stream on REPLACE without Content-Type, InvalidCopyDest for a no-op self-copy (allowed on versioned buckets as a restore), x-amz-copy-source-version-id, source ACLs and retention never carried over, and the 0-byte part MD5 all follow S3.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_pa.character: The UploadPartCopy slow path: re-streams a source range through the normal part-upload path whenever raw chunk copying would be wrong (encrypted source, encrypted upload, or a required checksum)
gotchas: SSE-S3 destinations go through putToFiler's multipart SSE-S3 branch, so copied parts inherit the per-part keystream reuse flagged on s3api_put_handlers.go.
applyRange skips to the start by reading and discarding bytes on SSE-S3 sources, so a copy of the tail of a large SSE-S3 object reads the whole prefix.
Content-MD5 is dropped on the cloned request, so the copied part is not integrity-checked against a client digest.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_pa.if_broken: Multipart objects assembled by copy are corrupt on read, or fail at completion for missing checksums.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_pa.ux: UploadPartCopy into encrypted or checksummed uploads produces readable objects; copying from SSE-KMS or SSE-C sources fails with 501.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_pa.what: Helpers decide when the slow path is needed: uploadEntryHasSSE, uploadEntryHasChecksum and sourceEntryIsEncrypted (SSE, or -encryptVolumeData cipher keys). openSourcePlaintextReader yields the source's plaintext for the byte range. SSE-S3 sources are decrypted per chunk (buildMultipartSSES3Reader) or via the legacy entry-level key and IV. Plain and volume-encrypted sources use a seekable chunk stream. SSE-KMS and SSE-C sources return errCopySourceSSEUnsupported. copyObjectPartViaReencryption wraps that reader in a cloned request (fakeContentRequest), stages the upload's SSE-KMS or SSE-S3 headers and base IV (applyDestSSEHeadersToCopyRequest) and its checksum algorithm, then calls putToFiler as a part write. Empty ranges become a 0-byte part. isTransientFilerError marks retryable filer errors for 503s.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_pa.when: CopyObjectPartHandler (UploadPartCopy) when the source is encrypted, the upload has SSE, or the upload requires a checksum.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_pa.why: Consequence: raw-copying source chunks into an encrypted upload left them under the source key while completion stamped destination SSE metadata on them, which gave deterministic corruption on GET (#8908). Design: re-using putToFiler means copied parts are encrypted, checksummed and ETagged exactly like uploaded parts. AWS compatibility: unsupported source types answer 501 NotImplemented rather than 500, so clients can tell a feature gap from a failure.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_st.character: The zero-buffer fast path for copying one chunk between volume servers: a source GET piped straight into a destination multipart POST
gotchas: Encrypted chunks always fall back to the buffered copySingleChunk path, so SSE copies do not get the memory savings.
The digest writer is skipped when the bytes are gzip; the caller must reuse the source chunk's ETag in that case.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_st.if_broken: Copied objects are corrupt (wrong encoding labels, truncated ranges), or copies leak goroutines and source bandwidth after failures.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_st.ux: Large server-side copies are faster and do not spike gateway memory.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_st.what: canStreamCopyChunk allows the path only for chunks with no SSE type and no per-chunk cipher key. streamCopyChunkRange sends a Range GET to the source volume, or for a whole chunk a GET with Accept-Encoding: gzip so stored gzip bytes pass through undecompressed. It feeds the body through an io.Pipe into a multipart/form-data POST to the destination volume, mirroring operation.upload_content's part headers, with Content-Encoding taken from the source response only. Plaintext bytes are optionally teed into a digest writer for the part ETag. A child context cancels both legs on any failure.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_st.when: Chunk-level copies in CopyObject and UploadPartCopy when the chunk needs no decryption or re-encryption.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_st.why: Consequence: UploadPartCopy and CopyObject of large objects (Harbor assembling image layers, for example) used to buffer every chunk, sometimes decompressing it, on the gateway and the volume server; heap profiles were dominated by that. Design: only the pipe's ~32 KiB is held per copy. Trusting the source's Content-Encoding rather than a caller hint keeps raw range bytes from being labelled gzip, which would corrupt reads.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_un.character: The CopyObject strategy dispatcher for encrypted objects: picks direct copy, key rotation, encrypt, decrypt or re-encrypt and runs the matching chunk copier
gotchas: Read-only buckets (quota) answer AccessDenied on copy, which callers may mistake for a permission problem.
The size calculation it logs is unused (see s3api_copy_size_calculation.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_un.if_broken: Copies produce unreadable objects, or metadata-only rotation leaves two entries sharing chunks so deleting one destroys the other's data.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_un.ux: aws s3 cp between encryption settings, or in place with new SSE headers, produces readable objects with the requested encryption.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_un.what: executeUnifiedCopyStrategy first resolves manifest chunks, detects the encryption state of source and destination (DetectEncryptionStateWithEntry), applies the destination bucket's default encryption when the request names none, and picks a strategy (DetermineUnifiedCopyStrategy). It then calls copyChunks, executeKeyRotation (SSE-KMS → SSE-KMS onto the same entry reuses the source chunks; everything else re-encrypts), executeEncryptCopy, executeDecryptCopy or executeReencryptCopy, which route to copyChunksWithSSEC, copyChunksWithSSEKMS or copyMultipartCrossEncryption. mapCopyErrorToS3Error maps read-only (quota) to AccessDenied and KMS/SSE-C errors to their codes. applyCopyBucketDefaultEncryptionHeaders writes a bucket default into request headers for paths that only read headers.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_un.when: CopyObjectHandler, when the source or destination involves SSE (s3api_object_handlers_copy.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_copy_un.why: Consequence: CopyObject is how clients rotate SSE keys, encrypt existing plaintext or move data between buckets with different defaults; picking the wrong strategy stores bytes under a key the metadata does not describe, so reads return garbage. Design: one dispatcher keeps the five transitions explicit. Handing back source chunks is only safe when the destination replaces the source entry, because nothing refcounts needles shared by two entries; a versioned rotation therefore re-encrypts. AWS compatibility: bucket default encryption applies to copies that do not request encryption, as on S3.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_delete..character: DeleteObject and DeleteObjects: the routing of a delete by versioning state, Object Lock checks, the If-Match condition, and per-key authorization for the batch API
gotchas: DeleteObjectHandler logs every delete at glog.Infof (not V-gated), which is noisy on busy buckets.
DeleteObjects reads the whole body with io.ReadAll and no cap; the 1000-key limit is checked only after decoding. Content-MD5, which AWS requires for this API, is not checked.
On the routed versioned path If-Match is checked before the delete, not atomically with it; only the lock fallback re-checks it under the lock.
A batch entry whose key normalizes to empty (only slashes) is reported as deleted.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_delete..if_broken: Locked versions get deleted, delete markers are missing or duplicated, or batch deletes remove keys the caller may not delete.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_delete..ux: aws s3 rm and batch deletes behave as on AWS, including versioned buckets and Object Lock.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_delete..what: DeleteObjectHandler checks the table-bucket path, the versionId against the bucket's versioning, the tag-conditioned policy and If-Match (checkDeleteIfMatch resolves the target by version and versioning state). It then takes the first path that applies. A trailing-slash key deletes a directory marker. An unversioned bucket uses a routed conditional delete on the key's owner filer. A versioned or suspended delete without versionId writes a delete marker (deleteVersionedObject; suspended deletes the null version first, then writes one null delete marker). A specific-version delete is routed with the WORM guards evaluated on the owner (governance bypass narrows the guard to COMPLIANCE); a delete marker is deleted without them, since markers carry no retention (#12592). Anything else falls back to the distributed object write lock with Object Lock enforcement. Responses carry x-amz-version-id and x-amz-delete-marker. DeleteMultipleObjectsHandler parses up to 1000 keys (a body that fails its signed payload hash answers that error, not 500, #12577) and, because the route only authenticated, authorizes each key with AuthorizeObjectDelete plus the tag-aware rechecks. It deletes each under the write lock (ETag as If-Match) and reports Deleted and Error entries, honoring Quiet.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_delete..why: Consequence: deletes are irreversible on unversioned buckets and decide what survives on versioned ones, so the routing has to respect versioning semantics and WORM protection on every path. Design: the common cases are routed to the key's owner filer under its per-path lock, avoiding the distributed lock round trip, and fall back to the lock path when the routed attempt does not settle. AWS compatibility: delete markers, the null version under Suspended, 204 for missing keys, per-key results in DeleteObjects, and AccessDenied for locked versions all follow S3.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_extract.character: A SeaweedFS extension that unpacks an uploaded zip archive into individual objects, triggered by ?extract=zip, a SeaweedFS header or the Snowball auto-extract metadata
gotchas: Members are extracted relative to the archive key's directory, not under a folder named after the archive.
Partial success is normal: the request answers 200 with per-member errors.
A checksum sent in an aws-chunked trailer is not available as a header or query value, so it is not verified against the archive.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_extract.if_broken: Archives are stored whole instead of unpacked, members escape the target prefix, or members are written without authorization.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_extract.ux: Uploading a .zip with the header unpacks it in place and returns a JSON report instead of an ETag.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_extract.what: isExtractZip detects the request. extractZipObject refuses explicit SSE headers, resolves (or auto-creates) the bucket, prepares the ACL and Object Lock headers, and verifies the archive's Content-MD5 and x-amz-checksum while spooling it (SpoolZipReader, with size limits). It then opens it as a zip (CheckZipLimits). For each member it sanitizes the name, authorizes the member key as its own PutObject (identity grant, table-bucket path, bucket policy, lock-header permissions, existing-object lock) and writes it through the normal versioned, suspended or plain put path with a MIME type from the extension. Directories become directory markers. The response is JSON listing extracted members and per-member errors, with a count header.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_extract.when: PutObject when isExtractZip(r) is true (also checked in bucket_paths.go routing).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_extract.why: Consequence: one upload creates many objects, so each must be authorized as if uploaded separately; otherwise a grant on the archive key would write anywhere under it. Design: members go through the same put functions as PutObject, so versioning, lifecycle TTL and checksums behave identically. Archive checksums are stripped from the request before members are written, since they describe the archive, not the members. AWS compatibility: the Snowball Edge auto-extract header is honored, so tools that use it work unchanged.

gotchas: Without versionId the latest version is changed and no x-amz-version-id is returned.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_legal_h.if_broken: Holds silently fail to apply, or apply to the latest version instead of the requested one.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_legal_h.ux: aws s3api put-object-legal-hold works as on AWS on Object Lock buckets.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_legal_h.what: Both handlers require Object Lock on the bucket (handleObjectLockAvailabilityCheck), re-run tag-conditioned bucket policies against the target object or version, and then call setObjectLegalHold / getObjectLegalHold (s3api_object_retention.go). Put parses and validates the LegalHold XML (ON/OFF), answers NoSuchKey for a missing object or version or one whose latest version is a delete marker (#12592), and echoes x-amz-version-id when one was given. Get maps a missing hold to NoSuchObjectLegalHold and a missing object or version to NoSuchKey.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_legal_h.why: Consequence: a legal hold blocks deletion of a version regardless of retention dates, so it is how data is preserved for litigation; setting it on the wrong version leaves the intended one deletable. Design: the policy recheck happens here because s3:ExistingObjectTag conditions can only be evaluated once the object's entry is loaded. AWS compatibility: status codes and the version header follow S3 and s3-tests.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list.go.character: ListObjects V1 and V2 over the filer's directory tree: S3 byte-order listing with prefixes, delimiters, markers and continuation tokens, folding versioned keys into their current state
gotchas: allow-unordered is accepted but the listing is always ordered.
Hidden-entry probes run under a per-prefix and a request-wide budget; beyond the budget a directory holding only deleted entries may still appear as a CommonPrefix.
A prefix object (content stored on a directory that also has children) can make a page run one item over max-keys, because its key and its CommonPrefix come from one entry.
Prefetched windows are read before the walk reaches them, so a key written into a directory after its window was read may be missing from that page, as with any non-snapshot listing.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list.go.if_broken: Keys are skipped or duplicated across pages, deleted objects reappear, or listings hang on deep directory trees.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list.go.ux: aws s3 ls, sync tools, and SDK paginators see the same keys, order and pagination as on AWS.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list.go.what: ListObjectsV2Handler and ListObjectsV1Handler parse and validate arguments (max-keys as uint16, allow-unordered not combined with a delimiter), adjust a marker that ends on the delimiter, call listFilerEntries, and answer NoSuchBucket only when the page is empty and the bucket is gone. Continuation tokens carry the raw key, or 'base64:' plus base64url when the key is not valid XML text, so a control character cannot be mangled to U+FFFD and skip keys. listFilerEntries normalizes prefix and marker to one directory (normalizePrefixMarker) and walks with doListFilerEntries; a listing without the '/' delimiter (a recursive walk) gets a listPrefetcher that reads the directories it will enter ahead of it. The walk defers each subdirectory until its '<name>/' block sorts, so output follows S3 byte order rather than filer name order. On a resumed page it starts strictly after the marker and looks up only the direct-child directories whose block can still hold keys past the marker, instead of re-listing from the marker's shortest prefix. A trailing-slash prefix is answered by looking that one directory up instead of listing every sibling it prefixes. It emits directory-key objects and prefix objects, folds keys into CommonPrefixes, hides .uploads and internal folders, and, for buckets with versioning configured, probes whether a directory holds only hidden or deleted entries. For versioned and suspended buckets it reconciles a base-path null object with its .versions sibling, retracting the null when the current version is a delete marker, settling pending nulls before a page closes. CommonPrefixes are sorted delimiter-aware and URL-encoded after sorting when encoding-type=url.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list.go.when: GET /<bucket>?list-type=2 (V2) and plain GET /<bucket> (V1, the catch-all bucket GET).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list.go.why: Consequence: listing is how every client discovers objects; a skipped key at a page boundary or a deleted key that still shows up breaks sync tools and backups silently. Design: S3 namespaces are flat but the filer is a tree, so the walk recreates flat byte ordering on top of directory listings and resumes from markers that may point into the middle of a subtree. A recursive walk of many small directories is one filer round trip per directory in series, so the prefetcher keeps several in flight (#12438); the marker lookups avoid rescanning a truncated subtree from its start (#12540), and the trailing-slash lookup avoids a sibling scan that SQL stores answer by reading the rest of the directory. Each failover attempt rebuilds the page from scratch so a half-built page never leaks into a retry. AWS compatibility: KeyCount, StartAfter, NextContinuationToken, EncodingType, CommonPrefix ordering ('foo/' before 'foo+1/'), and V1's Marker/NextMarker echo follow S3.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list.go.issue_note: On a bucket without versioning, a delimited listing reports an empty filer directory as a CommonPrefix, although no object exists under it. Deleting the last object under a prefix leaves the filer directories behind until the empty-folder cleaner removes them (about two minutes: DefaultQueueMaxAge plus a 30 s sweep), and dirHoldsOnlyHiddenEntries, which hides such prefixes, runs only when versioning is configured and keeps empty directories on purpose (TestEmptyDirectoryStaysACommonPrefix). AWS derives CommonPrefixes from existing keys only. Probed with boto3 on SeaweedFS 4.53 and master d51a7933: after deleting every object under job/task_1/p=0/ and job/task_1/p=1/, the recursive listing returns KeyCount=0, but a delimited listing still returns job/, task_1/, p=0/ and p=1/ (a versioned bucket returns nothing). Spark's default FileOutputCommitter v1 then fails an append with partitionBy within two minutes of an earlier write to the same table: its job commit finds the earlier job's empty _temporary/0/task_*/p=0 directory and S3A answers FileNotFoundException when it lists into it (reproduced 4/4 with Spark 3.5.7, Hadoop 3.3.4; passes on Silo's unversioned bucket, which lists no empty prefix).

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.character: S3ApiServer HTTP handlers for the multipart upload API (Create, UploadPart, Complete, Abort, ListParts, ListMultipartUploads); the storage logic lives in filer_multipart.go
gotchas: AbortMultipartUploadHandler calls s3err.WriteEmptyResponse (which already posts the audit log) and then s3err.PostLog again, so every abort emits two audit records.
Encryption parameters reach putToFiler as internal request headers (SeaweedFSSSEKMSBaseIVHeader, SeaweedFSSSES3KeyDataHeader…); this relies on iam.Auth scrubbing client-supplied copies.
Upload ids are deterministic per key (sha1 of the key) plus a random suffix; legacy ids without the suffix are still accepted.
getBucketMultipartResources / getObjectResources keep parsing after an invalid number and report the error code alongside a zero value.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.if_broken: Large uploads fail or complete into corrupted or undecryptable objects; aborted uploads leave orphan parts consuming storage.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.issue_note: NewMultipartUploadHandler passes isVersioningEnabled(bucket) as the objectLockEnabled argument of validateObjectLockHeaders (PutObject, CopyObject, POST policy and extract pass isObjectLockEnabled). On a versioning-enabled bucket WITHOUT Object Lock, x-amz-object-lock-mode/retain-until/legal-hold are therefore accepted (for callers holding the retention/legal-hold permission) instead of rejected; createMultipartUpload stores them on the upload entry and completion copies all upload-entry Extended keys onto the final object (filer_multipart.go). The object then reports retention in GET/HEAD headers and GetObjectRetention, but enforceObjectLockProtections skips buckets without Object Lock, so the 'locked' object can be deleted. Reproduced at b9866bae on a versioned bucket without Object Lock: PutObject with x-amz-object-lock-legal-hold answers 400, CreateMultipartUpload answers 200. Re-checked at 917cf534: unchanged (validateObjectLockHeaders still gets versioningEnabled at s3api_object_handlers_multipart.go:78).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.ux: aws s3 cp/sync and SDK multipart uploads of large files; ETags of parts; checksum algorithm echo on Create.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.what: NewMultipartUploadHandler validates key length, SSE headers, bucket (auto-creating if allowed), table-bucket layout, object-lock headers, Cache-Control/Expires and the upload ACL, then creates the upload. PutObjectPartHandler validates the upload id against the key (sha1(key) plus an optional _<32 hex> suffix), rejects an invalid x-amz-storage-class or x-amz-tagging before reading the body (validatePutHeaders), replays the upload's SSE-KMS or SSE-S3 parameters (key id, encryption context, base IV, key data) from the upload directory entry into internal request headers, enforces the upload's checksum algorithm, writes the part to <bucket>/.uploads/<uploadId>/<NNNN>_<uuid>.part through putToFiler (with the object's path as storage destination), then re-checks that the upload was not aborted meanwhile (cleaning up its own part if it was). Complete/Abort/List handlers parse parameters and delegate (a Complete body failing its signed payload hash answers that error rather than MalformedXML, #12577). Also: genUploadsFolder, genPartUploadPath, checkUploadId, getMultipartSSEAlgorithm (used by the bucket policy engine for s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption conditions on UploadPart).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.when: POST ?uploads, PUT ?partNumber&uploadId (without a copy source), POST ?uploadId, DELETE ?uploadId, GET ?uploadId, GET ?uploads.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_multipa.why: Consequence: multipart is how every large object (>5 GB, or above SDK thresholds) is written, so failures here break large uploads for all SDKs. Design: encryption is decided once at Create and replayed per part from the upload entry, so all parts share one key and base IV and the completed object decrypts as one stream (parts use offsets from the base IV, never re-evaluating bucket defaults). Part files get a UUID suffix so a retried UploadPart of the same number never overwrites a part still referenced by an in-flight complete. checkUploadStillOpen closes the race where an Abort lands while a part is being written, which would otherwise leave an orphan part. AWS compatibility: part numbers 1..10000, max-uploads/max-parts defaults of 10000, ListMultipartUploads with a key-marker outside the prefix answers NotImplemented.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_postpol.character: Browser-form uploads (POST /<bucket> multipart/form-data): signature check, POST policy enforcement, and the hand-off to the normal put paths
gotchas: Without a Policy field the upload proceeds with no conditions at all; with auth disabled it also proceeds unsigned.
content-length-range is checked only after the whole file has been received and spooled.
A form with no file part but a 'file' text field is treated as the file content.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_postpol.if_broken: Uploads bypass policy constraints or authorization, or browser uploads fail outright.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_postpol.ux: HTML forms and presigned POST from SDKs (generate_presigned_post) upload straight to SeaweedFS.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_postpol.what: PostPolicyBucketHandler reads the form (5 MiB in memory, the rest spooled), extracts the file and fields (each field capped at 1 MiB), substitutes ${filename} into Key, and validates the key. When auth is enabled it verifies the form's SigV2 or SigV4 signature (doesPolicySignatureMatch) and records the identity. It decodes and checks the Policy document (expiration and conditions via the policy package, content-length-range against the file size). It refuses acl and x-amz-acl fields that disagree, then drops every X-Amz-*, Cache-Control-family and Response-Content-Disposition header the client sent on the request itself (the policy signs only form fields) and copies the allowed form fields into their place; a value with control characters is MalformedPOSTRequest. It authorizes the write against a policy view of the request (putObjectACLPolicyRequest, so s3:x-amz-acl conditions see the form's ACL) and, when the form sets an ACL, the ACL write; with auth off, an ACL is still checked against the bucket policy. preparePostObjectACL turns the promoted acl / x-amz-grant-* fields into the owner and grants stored on the new object, applying ownership controls and BlockPublicAcls. Then it validates Object Lock headers and writes through the versioned, suspended or plain put path. The response is a 303 redirect (success_action_redirect, with bucket/key/etag in the query), 201 with a PostResponse XML, 200, or the default 204.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_postpol.why: Consequence: POST policies let a server hand a browser a signed, constrained upload ticket. If the conditions or the authorization were skipped, anyone holding the form could upload anywhere, at any size; if headers outside the form were honoured, the holder could add settings (ACL, SSE, metadata, lock) the signer never approved (#12585). Design: the request carries no Authorization header, so authentication comes from the form; after that the upload reuses the same put functions as PutObject, so versioning, SSE, lifecycle TTL, Object Lock and the stored ACL (#12567) behave identically. AWS compatibility: form field names, ${filename}, success_action_status / success_action_redirect and the error codes follow S3's POST Object.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.character: S3ApiServer HTTP handler (PutObjectHandler) plus putToFiler, the shared object-write engine reused by multipart parts, copy and versioned writes; also hosts conditional-header evaluation, object-lock header validation and bucket-default encryption/retention
gotchas: Internal metadata reaches putToFiler as request headers (ExtVersionIdKey, object-lock keys); this is only safe because iam.Auth scrubs client-supplied copies first (scrubInternalHeaders).
Bucket default encryption is skipped for multipart part writes (withMultipartPart context flag): encryption is decided at CreateMultipartUpload and replayed via headers.
lifecycleTTLSec is non-zero only for top-level non-versioned PutObject; parts and copy-parts must pass 0 or their TTL clock would start before completion.
Parts (object == "") are never manifestized because completion rebases chunk offsets, which manifest chunks cannot express.
updateLatestVersionInDirectory retries the .versions lookup 8 times with 100ms·2^n backoff (up to ~12.7s total) and refuses to move the latest pointer backwards to an older version id.
A routed PUT that a filer answers PRECONDITION_FAILED with a conditionAltKey is resent once against the entry the read path serves, for filers that ignore condition_alt_key.
partOffset is hardcoded to 0 for every SSE call, including multipart parts; for SSE-S3 this makes all parts of an upload share one keystream (see the s3api_put_handlers.go issue note).

validatePutHeaders runs twice on a PutObject: in the handler before the body is read (a PUT without Content-Type sniffs it from the first body read, so a later check would wait for the body) and again in putToFiler for its other callers (UploadPart, POST policy, zip members, UploadPartCopy).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.if_broken: Uploads fail or, worse, report success for objects that are not stored or that point at deleted chunks; versioned buckets lose versions; WORM retention is bypassed by overwrites; encrypted objects become unreadable.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.ux: What an S3 client sees on upload: ETag, x-amz-version-id, SSE and checksum echo headers, BadDigest / InvalidDigest / PreconditionFailed / IncompleteBody / ClientDisconnected / InvalidStorageClass errors, and 503 instead of a false success when a commit's outcome cannot be proven.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.what: PutObjectHandler validates the request (copy-source/partNumber misuse, Content-MD5, key length, table-bucket layout, conditional headers, bucket policy, SSE headers, the storage class and tag headers (validatePutHeaders, before anything reads the body), Cache-Control/Expires), then branches: a trailing-slash key ≤1KB becomes an explicit directory marker (mkdir under the object write lock; the marker keeps the storage class and tags; a Content-MD5 that does not match the empty body is BadDigest); otherwise it writes by versioning state (Enabled → putVersionedObject into <key>.versions/, Suspended → putSuspendedVersioningObject as the 'null' version, never-configured → plain putToFiler with an optional lifecycle TTL). putToFiler streams the body through MD5 and optional CRC/SHA hashers, applies SSE-C/KMS/S3 or bucket-default encryption, uploads chunks straight to volume servers (chunk size follows the filer's -maxMB, default 8 MiB), writes per-chunk SSE metadata, builds the entry (ETag, write id, checksum, owner, ACL, version id, lock fields, user metadata, tags, storage class; for a versioned write the finalize's newVersion hook re-mints the version id and file name just before the create, after the upload and lock wait, so ids follow commit order, #12454), manifestizes chunks, and commits: routed to the key's owner filer as an ObjectTransaction when possible, else CreateEntry under the distributed object write lock. Uncertain outcomes go through createAfterAmbiguousRoute / confirmCreateLanded before any chunk cleanup.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.when: PUT /bucket/key with no copy source or multipart query. putToFiler is also called by UploadPart (s3api_object_handlers_multipart.go), copy paths and the versioned and suspended helpers here. checkConditionalHeaders(ForReads) run in GET/HEAD/PUT/copy handlers.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_put.go.why: Consequence: PutObject is the main write path, and putToFiler is also the write core of UploadPart, CopyObject and versioned writes, so a regression here is data loss or corruption across all writes. Design: chunks upload on context.Background() so a client disconnect cannot leave a half-written object. A failed create does not prove the entry is absent (a lost reply can hide a commit, #11366; the filer can fail after inserting, #11387), so the entry's presence, not the error class, decides whether the uploaded chunks are orphaned. Recovery refuses to re-commit when a concurrent write superseded the entry or the chunks cannot be verified, because that would store an entry pointing at reclaimed needles. Each entry carries a fresh SeaweedFSWriteId because an empty object has no chunks to identify it. Conditional creates are never replayed once possibly sent: a lost commit followed by a delete would let IF_NOT_EXISTS recreate an entry whose chunks were already freed. AWS compatibility: a PutObject ETag is always the plain MD5 even when auto-chunked; object-lock headers require s3:PutObjectRetention / s3:PutObjectLegalHold, not just s3:PutObject; conditional headers follow RFC 7232 precedence; GET/HEAD on a missing key stays 404 under conditions; suspended versioning returns no x-amz-version-id.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_rename..character: RenameObject (PUT /<bucket>/<dst>?renameObject with x-amz-rename-source): a metadata-only move inside one bucket via the filer's AtomicRenameEntry, with idempotent retries
gotchas: The source is read and moved on the default filer, not the key's owner, so a PUT committed on the owner and not yet replicated can read as NoSuchKey.
Failing to stamp the client token does not stop the move; it only loses idempotency for that request.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_rename..if_broken: Objects vanish or the wrong object is moved, or a retry is answered as a missing source.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_rename..ux: Instant renames of large objects in unversioned buckets; retries after a timeout succeed instead of failing with NoSuchKey.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_rename..what: renameSourceCandidates reads x-amz-rename-source both as a bare key and, when prefixed with the bucket, as bucket/key, and pickRenameSource chooses the reading the bucket actually holds (only a proven absence moves on). The handler rejects trailing-slash keys and same-key renames, authorizes the source for both read and delete (with tag-aware rechecks), and refuses versioned buckets (NotImplemented). Under the write locks of both keys it re-reads the source, checks x-amz-rename-source-if-* and the destination conditions, stamps x-amz-client-token on the source so the move carries it, and moves the entry, handling keys that also have nested keys. retryRenameDecision answers a replay of a committed rename from the destination's token instead of NoSuchKey.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_rename..why: Consequence: a rename that loses data or moves the wrong object is worse than a failed one, and a client whose response was lost will retry. Design: the move is a filer rename, so bytes are never copied, and ETag, tags and SSE keys travel unchanged; the client token makes the operation idempotent within a validity window. Versioned buckets are refused because a move would have to rebuild the .versions chain. AWS compatibility: AWS offers RenameObject only on directory buckets; the header forms, conditions and error codes follow it.

gotchas: A missing retention answers ObjectLockConfigurationNotFoundError (AWS's code for this case), not a NoSuchRetention-style error.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_retenti.if_broken: Protected objects can have their retention shortened or removed, or legitimate extensions are refused.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_retenti.ux: aws s3api put-object-retention behaves as on AWS, including --bypass-governance-retention.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_retenti.what: Same shape as the legal-hold handlers: an Object Lock availability check, then the tag-conditioned policy recheck. PutObjectRetention also evaluates the governance-bypass request (the x-amz-bypass-governance-retention header plus s3:BypassGovernanceRetention), parses and validates the Retention XML, and calls setObjectRetention. Shortening or removing protected retention without that permission is ErrComplianceModeActive / ErrGovernanceModeActive, answered as AccessDenied. GetObjectRetention returns the stored mode and retain-until date, or ObjectLockConfigurationNotFoundError when none is set.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_retenti.why: Consequence: retention is the WORM guarantee: in COMPLIANCE mode nobody may shorten it, and in GOVERNANCE mode only callers holding the bypass permission may. A mistake here makes protected data deletable early. Design: the rules themselves live in s3api_object_retention.go; this file only handles HTTP and maps errors. AWS compatibility: the 403 on a forbidden change and the version header match S3 and s3-tests.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_tagging.character: Get/Put/DeleteObjectTagging for plain and versioned objects
gotchas: The versioned write is an unconditional whole-entry UpdateEntry, so a concurrent PutObjectRetention or legal-hold change on the same version can be reverted (the lost-update pattern flagged on s3api_bucket_policy_handlers.go).
PutObjectTagging reads exactly Content-Length bytes; a chunked request reads nothing and fails as MalformedXML.
Any error resolving a version, including a transient one, answers NoSuchKey.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_tagging.if_broken: Tag-based policies and lifecycle rules act on stale tags, or tags land on the wrong version.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_tagging.ux: aws s3api put-object-tagging and the version variants behave as on AWS.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_tagging.what: Each handler resolves the target by versioning state: the specific version, the latest version (delete markers answer NoSuchKey), or the plain entry read from the key's owner filer. It re-runs the bucket policy with the object's current tags (the version-specific action when versionId is given) and then reads or rewrites the X-Amz-Tagging-* xattrs. Put validates the Tagging XML (no duplicate keys, at most 10 tags). Unversioned writes go through setTags / rmTags on the owner filer; versioned writes rewrite the version entry with UpdateEntry on the owner, in the directory objectMetadataUpdateDirectory resolves.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_tagging.why: Consequence: object tags drive tag-conditioned bucket policies and lifecycle filters, so a tag change can grant or revoke access and change when objects expire. Design: the policy recheck uses the entry's current tags, because s3:ExistingObjectTag cannot be evaluated before the entry is loaded. A nested null version is updated in its own directory so a different object with the same basename is never rewritten. AWS compatibility: 10-tag limit, version-specific actions, and NoSuchKey on delete markers follow S3.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_lifecycle_ttl.go.character: The lifecycle TTL fast path: stamps a volume TTL on writes that a simple Expiration.Days rule covers
gotchas: Expiry is exactly write time + N×86400s, not AWS's rounding to the next midnight UTC.
The eligibility filter is duplicated in s3api_bucket_lifecycle_fastpath_warn.go and must stay in sync.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_lifecycle_ttl.go.if_broken: Objects expire early, late or never, or versioned history is wiped by TTL volumes.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_lifecycle_ttl.go.ux: Expiring data is reclaimed without the lifecycle worker scanning it; changing the rules later does not affect objects already written (see the fast-path warning header).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_lifecycle_ttl.go.what: NewLifecycleTTLResolver keeps only Enabled rules with ExpirationDays > 0, no tag filter, and a TTL that fits int32 seconds, converts them to compact (prefix, ttlSec, size bounds) rules sorted by ascending TTL, and returns nil for versioned buckets or when nothing qualifies. Resolve returns the TTL of the first rule whose prefix matches and whose size filter can be evaluated (unknown sizes skip size-filtered rules), or 0.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_lifecycle_ttl.go.when: Built when a bucket config is loaded with the fast-path flag on (s3api_bucket_config.go); Resolve runs on each PutObject / extract / POST write in an unversioned bucket.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_lifecycle_ttl.go.why: Consequence: a volume TTL makes the volume server reclaim expired data in bulk with no per-object delete, but it is decided at write time and cannot be taken back. Design: only predicates that cannot change after the write (prefix, size) are eligible; tag filters are left to the worker because tags can change. Versioned buckets are excluded because TTL volumes expire as a unit and would destroy noncurrent versions. The ascending sort makes the first match the shortest expiration, which is AWS's precedence for overlapping rules.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.character: S3ApiServer methods implementing object retention, legal hold and WORM enforcement, plus the XML types for Retention, LegalHold and ObjectLockConfiguration
gotchas: setObjectRetention and setObjectLegalHold are an unconditional read-check-write (getEntry → checks → updateEntry of the whole entry), not under the object write lock or an IF_ENTRY_EQUAL condition, so two concurrent retention updates race and a concurrent metadata change on the same entry can be overwritten.
getObjectEntry uses isVersioningEnabled (Enabled or object lock), so for Suspended buckets without a versionId it reads the plain object path.
A corrupt retention timestamp makes getObjectRetention fail, but enforceObjectLockOnEntry only logs it and treats the object as not under retention.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.if_broken: Locked objects can be deleted or overwritten (compliance violation), or unlocked objects become undeletable.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.ux: Clients see AccessDenied when deleting or overwriting locked data, and Get/PutObjectRetention / LegalHold behave like AWS's.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.what: get/setObjectRetention and get/setObjectLegalHold read and write ExtObjectLockModeKey / ExtRetentionUntilDateKey (unix seconds) / ExtLegalHoldKey on the right entry: the named version, the latest version file under .versions/ when versioning is enabled, or the plain object. setObjectRetention refuses to change the mode or shorten the date of a COMPLIANCE lock, and of a GOVERNANCE lock without bypass; it also stamps entry.WormEnforcedAtTsNs. enforceObjectLockOnEntry/Protections is the WORM gate used by deletes and overwrites: an active legal hold or COMPLIANCE retention always blocks, GOVERNANCE blocks unless x-amz-bypass-governance-retention: true AND the caller holds s3:BypassGovernanceRetention for that key. getObjectEntryForUpdate and the retention / legal-hold reads answer a delete marker (named or latest) as NoSuchKey / NoSuchVersion, and report a lookup failure that is not a genuine miss as itself rather than as not-found (missAs), so a transient filer error is a 5xx, not a NoSuchKey; a delete marker never counts as WORM-protected, so a lock recorded on one cannot keep it from being removed (#12592). Also: isObjectEntryMiss (a not-found that is not a transient Unavailable), the DefaultRetention XML unmarshaller that tracks whether Days/Years were present, and the Max retention limits (36500 days / 100 years).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.when: PUT/GET ?retention and ?legal-hold (the handlers in s3api_object_handlers_retention.go / _legal_hold.go); enforceObjectLockProtections from DeleteObject(s), non-versioned PutObject/overwrite paths, the directory-marker path, and lifecycle deletes (s3api_internal_lifecycle.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_retention.go.why: Consequence: this is the WORM guarantee; if it fails open, data under COMPLIANCE retention (which even admins must not delete) can be deleted or overwritten. Design: the bypass header alone is not enough: the permission is re-checked per key through authorizeObjectKeyAction, so a GOVERNANCE lock cannot be bypassed by anyone with plain write access. AWS compatibility: COMPLIANCE can only be extended, GOVERNANCE can be changed with bypass, legal hold is independent of retention; DaysSet/YearsSet distinguish 'absent' from '0' so Days=0 is rejected as InvalidRetentionPeriod, like AWS.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.character: S3ApiServer methods for read-your-writes lookups; holds a per-server TTL map of unreachable owners (s3a.unreachableOwners, sync.Map)
gotchas: routableWriteOwner (routed_write.go) is the single source of the owner; both sides must hash the same route key or reads miss writes.
The prior-owner probe happens only on ErrNotFound and only once; transport errors go through the normal failover walk instead.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.if_broken: Reads go to arbitrary filers and intermittently miss fresh writes or serve the old version; with the prior-owner probe broken, keys moved by a ring change briefly 404.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.ux: Read-after-write consistency in multi-filer deployments: a client that just PUT an object can GET it immediately.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.what: Reads an object's entry, or entries scoped to it (its .versions directory and version files), preferring the filer that owns the key's writes on the hash ring: getObjectEntryRoutedByKey, getObjectScopedEntryRoutedByKey, listObjectScopedEntriesRoutedByKey. If the owner says not-found during a rebalance it probes the key's prior owner once. Also keeps the 2s 'owner recently unreachable' marks and lookupEntryPreferringOwner / lookupEntryOnFiler for single-filer reads.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.when: GET/HEAD object and the versioning paths resolve entries through here when an objectWriteLockClient (ring) is configured; without one it reduces to plain getEntry/list.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_read.go.why: Consequence: with multiple filers, writes commit on the key's owner and replicate asynchronously; reading from any other filer right after a PUT could return 404 or the previous version. Design: unreachableOwnerTTL = 2s is long enough to spare a dead owner a dial on every request and short enough to resume owner-first reads soon after it or the ring recovers. lookupEntryPreferringOwner never swaps the owner for a healthier peer, since that would read behind the write the caller just made.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.character: S3ApiServer methods that turn object writes into ObjectTransaction RPCs on the key's owner filer, plus stateless builders for write conditions
gotchas: routeWriteCondition refuses to route a conditional write to a unique version path: a conditional versioned write must check the latest version, which only the lock path does.
routedObjectOwner deliberately returns no owner for versioned or object-lock buckets so WORM checks stay on the lock path.
routedUploadRemoval keeps a gateway-side exists() check because older filers ignore the mutation's upload-exists condition during rolling upgrades.
routedSelfCopy treats FailedPrecondition/NotFound as authoritative owner answers (no replay, owner not marked down).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.if_broken: Writes to the same key race (lost updates, both If-None-Match:* PUTs succeeding); a mismatched route key makes the filer forward to the wrong owner; a replayed transaction could re-apply mutations over a write that landed in between.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.ux: Concurrent writers to one key get consistent last-writer or precondition-failed answers instead of torn state; conditional PUTs behave like AWS's.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.what: Computes an object's ring route key (objectRouteKey), its owner filer (routableWriteOwner; routedObjectOwner for the unversioned-delete fast path) and sends atomic ObjectTransactions to it: routedPut (PUT plus optional finalize mutations such as RECOMPUTE_LATEST), routedMkFile/writeMultipartObject (multipart completion), routedDelete, routedSelfCopy (metadata-only copy guarded by IF_ENTRY_EQUAL). It turns HTTP conditional headers into filer WriteConditions evaluated under the owner's per-path lock (buildWriteCondition with RFC 7232 precedence; buildDeleteCondition honors If-Match only).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.when: PutObject, CompleteMultipartUpload, DeleteObject (unversioned fast path), CopyObject onto itself, and versioned finalize paths call these when routableWriteOwner returns an owner; with no objectWriteLockClient the callers fall back to the distributed-lock path and plain mkFile.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.why: Design: all writes to one object (versioned, suspended or not) share one route key and owner, so they serialize under one path lock and conditional writes (If-Match, If-None-Match: *) are checked atomically at the filer instead of racing in the gateway. A trailing-slash marker key ('dir/') hashes to the same owner as 'dir'. Transactions are not replayable: failover only crosses a channel that never came up, and each logical transaction carries one RequestId so a retry replays the recorded outcome instead of re-applying mutations. Multipart completion removes the upload directory inside the same transaction, with an upload-exists precondition, so an abort/lifecycle/s3.clean.uploads that removed the directory first fails the commit instead of publishing an object over freed chunks. Consequence: with a ring configured, this is how every routed object write lands.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.character: S3ApiServer helpers that resolve the ACL an object upload will carry (stashed in the request context) plus a stateless request rewriter for policy evaluation
gotchas: When auth is disabled but a bucket policy exists, an explicit ACL is still checked against the policy for both Write and WriteAcp.
putObjectACLPolicyRequest only rewrites requests that resolve to s3:PutObject; other actions pass through unchanged.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.if_broken: Objects are stored with the wrong owner or grants (public by mistake, or unreadable by the bucket owner), or ACL-conditioned bucket policies can be bypassed.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.ux: x-amz-acl / x-amz-grant-* on uploads behave like AWS's, including on presigned URLs; clear InvalidRequest / AccessControlListNotSupported errors.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.what: preparePutObjectACL runs before the object bytes are stored. It reads the canned ACL and x-amz-grant-* values from headers AND (for SigV4 presigned URLs) the query string, where presigners hoist signed headers; it rejects conflicting duplicates, requires s3:PutObjectAcl for any explicit ACL (with auth off, checks the bucket policy for Write and WriteAcp instead), and hands off to attachPutObjectACL. preparePostObjectACL is the POST Object variant: it reads only the headers the handler promoted from the form and does no authorization of its own, since PostPolicyBucketHandler already authorized the policy signer. attachPutObjectACL applies the bucket's ownership mode (BucketOwnerEnforced only accepts private / bucket-owner-full-control and makes the bucket owner the owner), always grants the owner FULL_CONTROL on custom grants, refuses AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers grants when the bucket blocks public ACLs (rejectPublicGrants; this covers PutObject, POST Object, CopyObject, CreateMultipartUpload and zip extract), and stashes the resulting owner/grant Extended attributes in the request context. applyPutObjectACL copies them onto the new entry. putObjectACLPolicyRequest builds a cloned request whose ACL headers carry the effective (query-hoisted, normalized) values so bucket-policy conditions such as s3:x-amz-acl evaluate the ACL the object will actually get, keeping the original values for s3:x-amz-grant-* conditions.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.when: PutObject (regular and directory-marker paths), POST Object (preparePostObjectACL), CreateMultipartUpload and other upload paths that call preparePutObjectACL before writing; putObjectACLPolicyRequest from iam.Auth (authRequestWithAuthType), checkPolicyWithEntry and the POST handler.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.why: Consequence: without this, a presigned URL could set an ACL through the query string that policy evaluation never saw (bypassing a 'Deny unless x-amz-acl=private' policy), or ACLs would be accepted on BucketOwnerEnforced buckets where AWS rejects them. Design: the ACL is computed once, before the upload, so a rejected ACL fails fast instead of after the body was stored; the context key cannot be set by clients. AWS compatibility: AccessControlListNotSupported for disallowed ACLs on BucketOwnerEnforced buckets; SigV2 requests ignore query-borne ACL values; canned and grant headers are mutually exclusive.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.character: S3ApiServer methods that build ObjectTransaction mutations for versioned writes and deletes on the key's owner filer (the routed counterpart of the gateway-side pointer updates in s3api_object_versioning.go)
gotchas: objectWriteOwner here and routableWriteOwner in s3api_object_routed_write.go both resolve the owner from the same route key; keep them in sync.
routedDeleteNullVersion falls back to the lock path on any transport or transaction error (deletes are idempotent), while routedDeleteSpecificVersion fails the request instead.
routedMultipartFinalize keeps a gateway-side upload-exists check for older filers that ignore the mutation's condition.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.if_broken: Latest pointers drift from the actual newest version, locked versions get deleted, or completed uploads leave their staging directories behind.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.ux: Read-after-write correct 'latest' in multi-filer clusters; AccessDenied when a versioned delete hits a locked version.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.what: latestPointerRecompute builds a RECOMPUTE_LATEST mutation: the filer scans <key>.versions/ (descending or ascending by version-id format), writes the winner's file name, size and mtime plus copies of its version id / ETag / owner / delete-marker / storage class onto the .versions entry, and optionally stamps NoncurrentSinceNs on the demoted version. On top of it: routedVersionedFinalize (delete markers: the marker entry is PUT into .versions/ in the same transaction as the recompute, so the scan sees it even when the gateway's own filer is not the owner, #12432), routedMultipartFinalize (PUT the version file + delete the upload dir + recompute, guarded by an upload-exists precondition), routedDeleteSpecificVersion (recompute only if the deleted file was current, then delete, under a WORM condition), routedDeleteNullVersion, versionedFinalize (a putFinalize that rides inside putToFiler's transaction, with an off-ring afterCreate fallback; its newVersion hook mints the version id and file name at commit, after the lock wait and the upload, so ids follow commit order rather than request arrival, #12454), finalizeSuspendedNullWrite, and wormDeleteCondition (legal hold not ON AND retention-until elapsed; with bypass, the retention clause is gated to COMPLIANCE only).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.when: Versioned PutObject / CopyObject (via putToFiler's finalize), CompleteMultipartUpload on versioned buckets, versioned DeleteObject with or without versionId, delete-marker creation, suspended-versioning null writes, whenever objectWriteOwner/routableWriteOwner returns an owner.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.why: Consequence: with a filer ring, these transactions are what keep the version file and the latest pointer consistent; without atomicity a crash or a concurrent writer leaves latest pointing at a missing or older version. Design: putting the version PUT, the pointer recompute and (for multipart) the upload-dir removal in ONE transaction under the object path lock means readers never see a half-finalized version; WORM conditions are evaluated by the filer under that same lock, so a retention set concurrently cannot be raced past. The off-ring path keeps the older lock-and-update behavior. AWS compatibility: governance bypass lifts only GOVERNANCE retention, never COMPLIANCE or legal hold.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.character: S3ApiServer methods implementing the on-filer versioning model (versions stored as <key>.versions/v_<id> files plus a latest-version pointer on the .versions directory entry), the ListObjectVersions handler, and a per-request filer retry budget
gotchas: getLatestObjectVersion retries the .versions lookup 8 times with 100ms·2^n backoff (worst case ~12.7s); conditional-header checks use the 1-retry fast path instead.
versionIdFromEntry falls back to the 'v_' file-name prefix when the entry has no version-id metadata.

The cached latest-version metadata on .versions/ is what listings trust; any writer that moves the pointer must call setCachedListMetadata or clearCachedVersionMetadata or listings show the old size/ETag.
processExplicitDirectory reports explicit directory markers as a 'null' version with the empty-content ETag d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.if_broken: Deleted objects reappear, the wrong version is served as current, ListObjectVersions duplicates or drops versions across pages, or lifecycle NoncurrentDays expiration fires at the wrong time.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.ux: x-amz-version-id semantics, delete markers, IsLatest flags and ordering in list-object-versions output, and whether deleting the latest version makes the previous one visible again.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.what: Owns the versioned storage layout: createDeleteMarker / createNullDeleteMarker write marker files under <key>.versions/ and move the latest pointer; when a ring owner exists, createDeleteMarker sends the marker entry itself in the routed finalize, so the marker and the RECOMPUTE_LATEST pointer flip commit in one transaction (#12432) instead of a marker written first and a flip that can fail after it; getSpecificObjectVersion / doGetLatestObjectVersion resolve a version or the current one; deleteSpecificObjectVersion repoints latest BEFORE deleting the version it names, and reports success for an entry already gone only when the filer confirms NotFound: lookups retry transient errors (retryFilerOp), a versions-directory lookup that still fails aborts the delete rather than risk a dangling pointer, and a failed delete whose recheck also fails returns the error so the caller can retry (#12482); updateLatestVersionAfterDeletion, healStaleLatestVersionPointer, clearStaleLatestVersionPointer and recoverLatestVersionWithoutPointer rescan .versions/ to repair a pointer naming a missing file, guarded by IF_ENTRY_EQUAL so a concurrent move is never overwritten. setCachedListMetadata copies the latest version's size/mtime/ETag/owner/storage-class/delete-marker onto the .versions entry so listings need one scan. ListObjectVersionsHandler walks the bucket (versionCollector with marker, prefix, delimiter and an early-stop bound) and interleaves Version/DeleteMarker/CommonPrefixes in AWS order. retryFilerOp retries transient filer errors 6 times (100ms doubling, capped at 2s) inside a shared per-request budget.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.when: GET/HEAD/DELETE/PUT on versioned or suspended buckets (via the object handlers and putVersionedObject), GET /bucket?versions, the versioning reconciler, and listing code that reads the cached latest metadata (getLatestVersionEntryFromDirectoryEntry).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.why: Consequence: this is the version history of every versioned bucket; a wrong pointer either resurrects a deleted object, hides the current one, or serves an old version. Design: the pointer moves before the version file is deleted so a crash in between never leaves latest naming a missing file; any stale pointer that does appear (replication lag, crashes) self-heals on read with an IF_ENTRY_EQUAL write and, failing that, is queued for the background versioning reconciler. NoncurrentSinceNs is stamped on the demoted version BEFORE the pointer flip, because the lifecycle router reacts to the flip's metadata event and would otherwise derive the age from a sibling's mtime (wrong for versioned copies). A suspended-versioning delete collapses onto one 'null' marker (v_null) rather than accumulating markers, per the S3 spec. AWS compatibility: ListObjectVersions sorts by key, then newest version first, interleaving the three element kinds; max-keys caps at 1000 and max-keys=0 returns an empty, non-truncated page.

weed/s3api/s3api_path_validation.go.character: The bucket-route guard that rejects path traversal, empty path vars, ambiguous subresources and unsafe versionId/uploadId values before any handler runs
gotchas: operationSubresources must be kept in sync with new subresource routes; bucketQueryActions keys are counted automatically, others are not.
hasPathSegmentQuery uses a substring test on the raw query ('versionId' anywhere) as a fast path, then the exact keys are checked.
weed/s3api/s3api_path_validation.go.if_broken: Cross-bucket reads and writes that bypass authorization, or version and upload IDs that address arbitrary filer paths.
weed/s3api/s3api_path_validation.go.ux: Normal clients never notice; crafted paths get 400 InvalidRequest.
weed/s3api/s3api_path_validation.go.what: validateRequestPath checks the mux vars: bucket must be a valid bucket name and object a valid key, both non-empty. If the request has a query, it rejects two operation subresources (hasAmbiguousSubresource over operationSubresources plus every bucketQueryActions key), and versionId / uploadId values that are not valid single path segments (hasPathSegmentQuery also catches percent-encoded spellings of those keys).
weed/s3api/s3api_path_validation.go.when: Every request matched by the per-bucket subrouter (bucket.Use(validateRequestPath) in registerRouter).
weed/s3api/s3api_path_validation.go.why: Consequence: the router runs with SkipClean(true), so '..' survives routing and util.JoinPath later collapses it. Without this guard 'GET /bucket-A/../evil-bucket/k' is authorized against bucket-A but read from evil-bucket. versionId and uploadId become filer entry names, so a value containing '/' or '..' would also escape its directory. Design: one middleware on the bucket subrouter, so every bucket and object route gets the check without each handler repeating it.

weed/s3api/s3api_public_access_block.go.character: S3 Block Public Access for one bucket: the PublicAccessBlockConfiguration type, its strict XML parser, and rejectPublicGrants, the check every ACL-writing path runs when the bucket blocks public ACLs
gotchas: Only BlockPublicAcls and IgnorePublicAcls are enforced. BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets are parsed, stored and returned by GetPublicAccessBlock, but nothing reads them (see issue note).
A stored configuration that fails to parse is treated as all four flags true (fail closed) by newBucketConfigFromEntry.
weed/s3api/s3api_public_access_block.go.if_broken: Public ACLs slip into protected buckets, or ordinary uploads with private ACLs start failing.
weed/s3api/s3api_public_access_block.go.issue_note: BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets are accepted and stored but never enforced. The only code that sets them is the fail-closed fallback in s3api_bucket_config.go, and nothing reads them. On S3, BlockPublicPolicy makes PutBucketPolicy refuse a policy that grants public access, and RestrictPublicBuckets limits a public policy to service principals and the owner's account. Here a client (for example Terraform's aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block with all four true) is told the bucket is protected while public policies still work. Probe (newPublicAccessBlockTestServer, bucket entry storing all four flags true): getBucketConfig reports BlockPublicPolicy=true, and PutBucketPolicy with Effect Allow, Principal "*", Action s3:GetObject answers 204.
weed/s3api/s3api_public_access_block.go.ux: x-amz-acl: public-read on a protected bucket answers 403, while private and account grants keep working (clients that send x-amz-acl: private on every upload are unaffected).
weed/s3api/s3api_public_access_block.go.what: PublicAccessBlockConfiguration holds the four AWS flags (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets). parsePublicAccessBlock decodes the XML and refuses any unknown element, then clears the namespace so the stored form is canonical. blocksPublicAcls / ignoresPublicAcls are nil-safe accessors. hasPublicGrant reports a grant to the AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers group. rejectPublicGrants answers AccessDenied when the bucket's config blocks public ACLs and the grants contain a public one; the configuration itself is stored on the bucket entry (Seaweed-X-Amz-Public-Access-Block) and carried in the cached BucketConfig (s3api_bucket_config.go).
weed/s3api/s3api_public_access_block.go.when: On every ACL-bearing write in a bucket with BlockPublicAcls; when Put/Get/DeletePublicAccessBlock run; when a bucket config is loaded.
weed/s3api/s3api_public_access_block.go.why: Consequence: Block Public Access is how operators make sure a bucket cannot be opened to the internet by an ACL, whatever a client sends; a check that misses one ACL path defeats it. Design: one helper is called by every path that writes ACLs (preparePutObjectACL for PutObject, CopyObject, CreateMultipartUpload and zip extract; PutObjectAcl; PutBucketAcl; POST Object), so they cannot disagree. Unknown elements are refused because a misspelled BlockPublicAcl would otherwise be stored as false. Compatibility: the XML shape, the AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers definition of 'public' and AccessDenied follow S3.

weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.character: S3ApiServer methods: the single SSE dispatch point for writes (SSE-C, SSE-KMS, SSE-S3, single-part and multipart) and the SSE-metadata writer for entries
gotchas: Order matters: the three handlers are applied in sequence on the same reader; request validation elsewhere must keep SSE-C and SSE-KMS/S3 mutually exclusive, or data would be double-encrypted.
Fixing the IV scheme requires a matching change in completedMultipartChunk (filer_multipart.go) and must stay readable for objects already written with partOffset 0.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.if_broken: Encrypted objects become unreadable, or are encrypted unsafely.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.issue_note: SSE-S3 multipart parts reuse the AES-CTR keystream. handleSSES3MultipartEncryption encrypts every part with the upload's single shared DEK and CreateSSES3EncryptedReaderWithBaseIV(baseIV, partOffset), and putToFiler always passes partOffset = 0 (s3api_object_handlers_put.go; completedMultipartChunk in filer_multipart.go documents and depends on this). So byte k of every part is XORed with the same keystream byte, and anyone with read access to the stored chunks (the threat SSE-S3 exists for) can XOR two parts to obtain the XOR of their plaintexts. s3_constants.PartOffsetMultiplier, documented as preventing exactly this, is never used. SSE-KMS is unaffected (fresh data key per part) and SSE-C uses a random IV per part.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.ux: Invisible when correct: clients get the matching SSE response headers and can read their data back.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.what: handleAllSSEEncryption chains the three handlers over the body reader and reports which type applied. handleSSECEncryption parses the customer key and encrypts with a random IV; handleSSEKMSEncryption builds the encryption context (bucket/key plus any user context) and either encrypts with a fresh data key and random IV, or, for multipart parts (SeaweedFSSSEKMSBaseIVHeader set by the part handler), with a fresh data key and the upload's base IV advanced by partOffset; handleSSES3Encryption encrypts single-part objects with a fresh DEK and random IV, or multipart parts with the upload's shared DEK (SeaweedFSSSES3KeyDataHeader) and base IV advanced by partOffset. storeSSEMetadata writes the object-level SSE keys (IV and key MD5 for SSE-C, serialized key metadata plus algorithm/key id for SSE-KMS and SSE-S3).
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.when: putToFiler (PutObject, UploadPart, copy destinations) and the directory-marker path of PutObjectHandler.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.why: Consequence: every encrypted write goes through here; it decides the IV and key each byte is encrypted with, and therefore whether reads can decrypt and whether the encryption is sound. Design: multipart parameters are injected as internal headers by the part handler so one code path serves PutObject and UploadPart; SSE-KMS uses a new data key per call, so reusing an IV across parts is harmless there. AWS compatibility: SSE-C, SSE-KMS (with x-amz-server-side-encryption-context) and SSE-S3 behave as in AWS from the client's point of view.

weed/s3api/s3api_put_object_helper.go.character: The request-body front end for uploads: decodes SigV4 streaming framing and verifies a declared x-amz-content-sha256 as the body streams
gotchas: The mismatch is only known after the whole body has been read and uploaded as chunks; the caller has to clean those chunks up.
On mismatch the last Read returns its bytes with a nil error and the next Read returns the error, so a reader that stops at n == 0 without checking the error would miss it.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_object_helper.go.if_broken: Bodies that do not match their signed hash are stored, or valid uploads fail.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_object_helper.go.ux: A corrupted or tampered upload fails with XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch instead of storing bad data.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_object_helper.go.what: getRequestDataReader returns the body to store. It first unwraps a body bindSignedPayload bound, taking the signed hash with it. For streaming (signed or unsigned) uploads the body is the chunked reader from newChunkedReader. If a real hash is known (the bound one, else x-amz-content-sha256 as hex or base64; the streaming and UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD sentinels are skipped), the body is wrapped in contentSha256Verifier, which hashes everything read and turns EOF into a mismatch error when the digest differs. An empty body is checked at once because handlers may never read it. An undecodable header value is InvalidArgument.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_object_helper.go.when: PutObject (putToFiler) and UploadPart, before the body is chunked into volume servers.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_object_helper.go.why: Consequence: SigV4 signs the declared hash, not the body, so without this check a client (or a proxy in between) can send different bytes under a valid signature. Design: verifying while streaming keeps uploads constant-memory; the error surfaces at EOF, so the upload path must treat a late read error as a failed upload. AWS compatibility: XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch as on S3, and chunked streaming is decoded even when IAM is off, so SDK defaults work against an open gateway.

weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.character: The composition root: S3ApiServerOption (flags), the S3ApiServer struct every handler hangs off, its constructor and the mux route table; plus the bucket-policy recheck helpers handlers call after loading an entry
gotchas: Inserting a route in the wrong position silently shadows others; follow the ordering rule in the comment at the top of the per-bucket route block.

No bucket configuration write runs under plain ACTION_WRITE any more: lifecycle, request payment, encryption, public access block, ownership controls and CreateBucket require ACTION_ADMIN (#12327); policy, CORS, versioning (#12433), object lock, quota, tagging and ACL each have their own action.
Ownership-controls routes skip cb.Limit (they are wrapped only in iam.Auth).
ValidateS3Credential compares the secret with != (not constant time); lance/handlers_oauth.go uses it for OAuth client_credentials and token verification.

STS has its own routes plus a lowest-priority unauthenticated POST / fallback; signed POST / goes to UnifiedPostHandler, which dispatches on Action (AssumeRole*/GetCallerIdentity/GetFederationToken to STS, everything else to embedded IAM).
recheckPolicyForKeyWithLookup is deny-biased: any lookup miss or error keeps the original Deny, and an explicit Deny in the caller's own policies still vetoes a bucket-policy Allow.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.if_broken: The gateway does not start, or routes land on the wrong handler (for example a tagging PUT treated as a PutObject that overwrites the object). If the lock-ring subscription were lost, route-by-key writes would silently fall back to the distributed lock path.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.issue_note: ValidateS3Credential compares the client-supplied secret with cred.SecretKey using != (s3api_server.go:1541), which returns at the first differing byte. It is the credential check behind the Iceberg and Lance OAuth client_credentials token endpoints (iceberg/handlers_oauth.go, lance/handlers_oauth.go), where the raw secret arrives in the request, so response timing leaks how much of a guessed secret is correct. Both signature paths in this package use subtle.ConstantTimeCompare (auth_signature_v4.go, auth_signature_v2.go). The OAuth handlers already answer every failure with the same generic message, so the timing is the only leak. Low severity, since network jitter makes the attack slow; the fix is a one-line constant-time compare. Found by reading; not reproduced.
