weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.ux: Defines which URL shapes work (path-style vs virtual-host via -domainName, health probes at /status, /healthz, /readyz), which operations exist, and the defaults: no IAM config means 'no credentials = allow all' so `docker run seaweedfs` works out of the box (#9557), while an explicit IAM config file defaults to Deny.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.what: NewS3ApiServerWithStore wires the whole gateway: legacy IAM (IdentityAccessManagement), bucket policy engine, FilerClient (with master-based filer discovery when -master is given), the object-write lock ring (LockClient fed by master LockRingUpdates), the SSE-S3 key manager, a shared ReaderCache for GET streaming (256 downloader slots, optional in-memory chunk cache), circuit breaker, bucket config cache (60 min TTL), optional advanced IAM + STS + embedded IAM API, trusted proxies, SIGHUP reload hooks, and the background loops (metadata subscription, bucket size metrics, owner-index backfill, versioning reconciler). registerRouter declares every S3 route on gorilla/mux: path-style and virtual-host routers per -domainName plus a host-less catch-all, each wrapped as track(iam.Auth(cb.Limit(handler, ACTION))). It also holds checkPolicyWithEntry / recheck*Policy*, which re-run bucket-policy evaluation once a handler has the object's entry (for s3:ExistingObjectTag conditions) and refuse a key that names a version file's physical path, so signed GET, HEAD, copy sources and object subresources cannot read a version past s3:GetObjectVersion or a Deny on the logical key (#12574); the lookup-based recheck fetches the entry whenever the key has that shape, even in a bucket without a policy, and small adapters other servers use (AuthenticateRequest, ValidateS3Credential, GetCredentialByAccessKey).
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.when: Constructed once at process start by weed/command (s3, filer -s3, mini); registerRouter runs inside the constructor. The recheck helpers run inside object handlers after the entry is fetched. SIGHUP re-reads the -config identities, the JWT filer signing keys and the trusted proxies.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.why: Design: route order is load-bearing: gorilla/mux picks the first match, so object routes with a query come before plain object routes, those before bucket routes with a query, and plain bucket routes come last. ListObjectsV1 is the catch-all GET and explicitly answers NotImplemented for unrouted subresources instead of returning a listing. The lock client subscribes to ring updates BEFORE the master loop starts because the master sends the initial LockRingUpdate only once per connect. The advertised host must be -ip, not a wildcard bind address, or IAM pushes from peers dial an unroutable address and fail silently after 10s. The auth path primes bucket loads (iam.primeBucketForIAM) because advanced-IAM evaluates the bucket-policy mirror before any handler runs, and a grant carried only by a not-yet-mirrored policy would otherwise deny forever. Consequence: everything else in the package is reached from here.

weed/s3api/s3api_server_grpc.go.character: The gateway's gRPC IAM cache service (SeaweedS3IamCache): one-way pushes of identities, policies and groups from the filer or admin tooling into this gateway's in-memory IAM
gotchas: Without a signing key the service is open to every local peer, including other processes on the same host.
GetPolicy answers an empty response, not NotFound, for an unknown policy.
PutIdentity and RemoveIdentity do not check s3a.iam for nil, unlike the policy and group RPCs.
weed/s3api/s3api_server_grpc.go.if_broken: Gateways keep serving revoked keys until a full reload, or anyone who can reach the gRPC port rewrites identities.
weed/s3api/s3api_server_grpc.go.ux: IAM changes made anywhere show up on all gateways almost immediately.
weed/s3api/s3api_server_grpc.go.what: Implements PutIdentity / RemoveIdentity, PutPolicy / DeletePolicy / GetPolicy / ListPolicies and PutGroup / RemoveGroup on top of IdentityAccessManagement (UpsertIdentity, RemoveIdentity, PutPolicy…). Every RPC first runs checkAdminAuth. If a filer signing key (jwt.filer_signing.key) is configured, the caller must present 'Bearer <JWT>' signed with it as admin claims (no SessionId, no path or method scope); the shared security.CheckGrpcAdminToken accepts the request if any of its first 4 authorization values is such a token, so a stale token the context carries ahead of a fresh one no longer fails the call (#12397). With no key, only local peers (unix socket, loopback, the server's own addresses) are accepted.
weed/s3api/s3api_server_grpc.go.when: When the filer or the embedded IAM API on another gateway propagates a targeted change (credential manager's propagating store); GetPolicy and ListPolicies for tooling.
weed/s3api/s3api_server_grpc.go.why: Consequence: these calls rewrite who can authenticate, so an unauthenticated caller could add an admin identity. Design: the filer propagates a single changed identity or policy to every gateway, so an IAM change takes effect in seconds without each gateway reloading the whole configuration. The auth mirrors the filer's own IamGrpcServer.checkAdminAuth, so one operator setting secures both.

weed/s3api/s3api_sosapi.go.character: Smart Object Storage API (SOSAPI) virtual objects that let backup software (such as Veeam) discover capabilities and capacity
gotchas: Used space is the sum of raw volume sizes, which still counts un-vacuumed garbage, while quota enforcement uses LogicalSize; a bucket can look full here before quota enforcement agrees.
Each capacity.xml request pulls the full topology from a master, the cost bucket_size_metrics.go avoids by asking for CollectionStatistics.
On error the response reports zero capacity instead of failing.
weed/s3api/s3api_sosapi.go.if_broken: Backup software reports zero or wrong capacity and may refuse to write.
weed/s3api/s3api_sosapi.go.ux: Veeam-style repositories show capacity and free space for SeaweedFS buckets.
weed/s3api/s3api_sosapi.go.what: Two virtual keys under a well-known UUID folder: system.xml (protocol version, model, CapacityInfo capability, recommended 4 MB block size) and capacity.xml. generateCapacityXML reports the bucket quota as capacity when one is set, otherwise the cluster capacity from the master topology (calculateClusterCapacity caps slot counts by physical disk counters), with used bytes summed from the bucket collection's volumes. handleSOSAPIGetObject / HeadObject serve them from the object GET/HEAD handlers.
weed/s3api/s3api_sosapi.go.when: GET/HEAD of the SOSAPI paths inside any bucket, after normal authorization.
weed/s3api/s3api_sosapi.go.why: Consequence: backup products size their jobs and fail early on full repositories using these numbers. Design: the files are generated on demand, so they always reflect current capacity and never exist on disk. AWS compatibility: none; SOSAPI is a vendor protocol on top of S3.

gotchas: /readyz is ready even when the filer is unreachable, so traffic is routed to a gateway that will answer 500s.
weed/s3api/s3api_status_handlers.go.if_broken: Orchestrators restart or drain healthy gateways.
weed/s3api/s3api_status_handlers.go.ux: Probes succeed whenever the process is up.
weed/s3api/s3api_status_handlers.go.what: StatusHandler answers 200 with an empty body on /status, /healthz and /readyz. With ?features it answers JSON {"sseS3": <bool>} saying whether the SSE-S3 key manager is configured; the admin UI's vector encryption page probes it before offering SSE-S3 (#12517).
weed/s3api/s3api_status_handlers.go.when: GET/HEAD /status, /healthz and /readyz, registered ahead of the bucket routes and outside iam.Auth.
weed/s3api/s3api_status_handlers.go.why: Consequence: load balancers and Kubernetes probes mark the gateway healthy or not based on this answer. Design: it checks nothing (no filer or master round-trip), so a probe never fails because of backend latency; it reports only that the HTTP server is serving.

weed/s3api/s3api_sts.go.character: STSHandlers: the AWS STS query-API front end served on the S3 port (one instance when advanced IAM has an STS service), with its XML response types
gotchas: The direct STS routes are not wrapped in iam.Auth, so internal headers are not scrubbed before verifyV4Signature; extractSessionToken prefers the internal X-SeaweedFS-Session-Token header, which a client could send unsigned instead of the signed X-Amz-Security-Token (the token itself must still be valid for the signed access key).
GetFederationToken with no Policy gives the federated session all of the caller's attached policies; AWS documents that such a session has no permissions unless a session policy is passed.
When several LDAP providers exist and LDAPProviderName is omitted, the first one found is used (logged as non-deterministic).
AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity delegates to the IAM manager when present so role-store roles are visible, otherwise to the bare STS service.
weed/s3api/s3api_sts.go.if_broken: Federated users cannot obtain credentials, or obtain credentials for roles or permissions they should not have.
weed/s3api/s3api_sts.go.ux: aws sts assume-role(-with-web-identity), get-caller-identity and get-federation-token work against SeaweedFS.
weed/s3api/s3api_sts.go.what: HandleSTSRequest dispatches on Action (API version 2011-06-15): AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity (OIDC token → role via the IAM manager, typed errors for expired/invalid tokens), AssumeRole (SigV4-signed caller; role trust policy and explicit identity denies checked; an empty RoleArn means 'assume self', allowed only with a global sts:AssumeRole grant, admins get an is_admin claim; the session records the caller as its user (ExternalUserId: the caller's name, or for a caller that is itself an STS session, that session's aws:username), so policies see aws:username as the user and not the caller-chosen session name, #12572), AssumeRoleWithLDAPIdentity (username/password checked against the configured or first LDAP provider, then the role's trust policy), GetFederationToken (long-term credentials only; the federated session carries the caller's attached and stored policies plus an optional session policy), GetCallerIdentity. prepareSTSCredentials resolves the role (cap by its MaxSessionDuration), mints a session id, JWT session token (with role, session name, attached policies, session policy) and temporary access/secret keys. Validates RoleSessionName (2–64 chars, [\w+=,.@-]), DurationSeconds (900s .. 12h or the configured max; federation up to 36h) and the session policy; reports PackedPolicySize against a 2048-byte budget.
weed/s3api/s3api_sts.go.when: POST / with Action=… on the S3 port: explicit query routes, the authenticated IAM/STS UnifiedPostHandler, and a lowest-priority unauthenticated fallback (for AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity/LDAP bodies).
weed/s3api/s3api_sts.go.why: Consequence: STS is how OIDC/LDAP users and applications obtain temporary S3 credentials; a flaw here mints credentials for roles the caller should not get. Design: trust policies are always checked against the caller's principal ARN, and an explicit Deny in the caller's own policies still blocks AssumeRole; temporary credentials are self-contained JWTs, so any gateway sharing the signing key can validate them without shared session storage. AWS compatibility: action names, parameter names, error codes, XML envelopes and duration limits mirror AWS STS so SDKs and the aws CLI work unchanged.

weed/s3api/s3api_subresource_ambiguity.g.character: A router-wide middleware that refuses requests naming more than one operation subresource
gotchas: The AST shows no callers (in=0) because the function is passed as a value to router.Use in s3api_server.go; it is not dead.
weed/s3api/s3api_subresource_ambiguity.g.if_broken: An authorization-confusion hole: a caller allowed one operation could run another by adding a second subresource.
weed/s3api/s3api_subresource_ambiguity.g.ux: Clients never send two subresources legitimately; a crafted request gets 400.
weed/s3api/s3api_subresource_ambiguity.g.what: rejectAmbiguousSubresource answers InvalidRequest when hasAmbiguousSubresource finds two or more operation-selecting query keys (policy, tagging, acl, versioning, uploads…), otherwise passes the request on.
weed/s3api/s3api_subresource_ambiguity.g.when: Every request, through router.Use in registerRouter, before any route matches.
weed/s3api/s3api_subresource_ambiguity.g.why: Consequence: gorilla/mux picks a route by registration order while the IAM action resolver checks the query in its own order, so 'PUT /bucket?policy&tagging' could be authorized as PutBucketTagging and served as PutBucketPolicy. Design: validateRequestPath already enforced the rule inside the bucket routes; registering it on the root router covers the routes outside them (STS, IAM, S3 Tables, health) and runs once per request.

weed/s3api/s3api_tables.go.character: The gateway glue for S3 Tables: route registration (JSON target and REST paths), the authentication wrapper, and request builders that turn REST paths into handler payloads
gotchas: Views, UpdateTable, RegisterTable and UpdateNamespace still have no REST routes; they are reachable only through the X-Amz-Target JSON route (which the Iceberg REST layer uses through Manager). A REST call for one of them now gets 404 UnknownOperationException rather than being taken as an S3 request.
Clients must sign with service 's3tables'; a request signed for 's3' never matches the REST routes or the catch-all.
weed/s3api/s3api_tables.go.if_broken: S3 Tables calls 404, ordinary S3 requests are misrouted into the catalog, or an s3tables-signed call for an unrouted operation is run as an S3 PUT that stores the body as an object and reports success.
weed/s3api/s3api_tables.go.ux: aws s3tables CLI commands (REST) and SDKs using the JSON protocol both work against the S3 endpoint.
weed/s3api/s3api_tables.go.what: registerS3TablesRoutes builds an S3TablesApiServer around s3tables.S3TablesHandler, wiring the SSE-S3 availability check, the local-account predicate, default-allow (true when advanced IAM is absent) and the IAM authorizer. It registers POST / with X-Amz-Target: S3Tables.* plus REST routes for buckets, namespaces, tables (including PUT .../{namespace}/{name}/rename for RenameTable), policies, maintenance, tags and get-table. Every REST route requires a SigV4 credential scope whose service field is exactly 's3tables' (isS3TablesSignedRequest splits AK/DATE/REGION/SERVICE/aws4_request, so a region named s3tables does not match); this keeps them from colliding with ordinary buckets named 'buckets' or 'tables'. A request signed for s3tables that no route took is answered 404 UnknownOperationException by a catch-all registered after them, instead of falling through to the /{bucket} routers. authenticateS3Tables authenticates only (AuthSignatureOnly) and leaves authorization to the handler. The build*Request functions decode path parameters, query parameters and JSON bodies into the s3tables request types; buildRenameTableRequest takes the source from the path and the optional newNamespaceName/newName from the body, requiring at least one.
weed/s3api/s3api_tables.go.when: Router setup in registerRouter; then every S3 Tables request.
weed/s3api/s3api_tables.go.why: Consequence: the S3 Tables API shares the S3 port, so any route overlap would let an S3 request reach the catalog or the other way round. Design: the service-scope matcher removes ambiguity without relying on content types an anonymous S3 request could set. Authorization stays in the s3tables package, which knows owners and resource policies.

weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.character: Stateless helpers (plus two thin S3ApiServer path methods) defining the version-id format and its ordering
gotchas: Do not compare version ids with plain string comparison: old- and new-format ids sort in opposite directions; always use compareVersionIds.
If crypto/rand fails, the random half falls back to 16 zeros (logged), so ids generated in the same nanosecond could collide.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.if_broken: Latest-version selection picks the wrong version (older data served as current, deleted objects resurrected), or a crafted versionId escapes the .versions directory.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.ux: Clients see 32-hex-char x-amz-version-id values; ListObjectVersions orders newest first.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.what: generateVersionId builds a 32-hex-char id: 16 hex of a nanosecond timestamp plus 16 hex of crypto randomness. The NEW format stores MaxInt64−now ('inverted', so newer ids sort first lexicographically); the OLD format stores now directly. isNewFormatVersionId tells them apart by the 0x4000000000000000 threshold, compareVersionIds orders any mix (same format: lexicographic, in the right direction; mixed: by decoded timestamp; 'null' always last), getVersionIdFormat keeps an object on the format its .versions/ latest pointer already uses (defaults to new). Also getVersionedObjectDir (<bucket>/<key>.versions), getVersionFileName (v_<id>), isValidVersionID (a safe single path segment).
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.when: Every versioned write (putVersionedObject, delete markers, versioned copy/complete), every latest-version selection, and validation of any client-supplied versionId.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.why: Consequence: version ids are filer path segments and the sort key for 'latest' everywhere (pointer recompute, ListObjectVersions, NoncurrentVersion lifecycle); a wrong comparison promotes an old version to current. Design: inverted timestamps make the filer's natural ascending listing return newest first, so finding the latest needs no full scan, while objects whose history predates the change keep their old ascending format so their ordering stays consistent. isValidVersionID rejects '/', '\', '.', '..' because a version id becomes a filename under .versions/ (path traversal). AWS compatibility: AWS version ids are opaque strings; 'null' is the reserved id for unversioned / suspended writes.

weed/s3api/s3api_versioning_reconciler.g.character: A background queue that repairs .versions directories whose latest-version pointer names a missing file
gotchas: The queue is per process and in memory: a restart loses pending candidates, and the read-path heal remains the safety net.
Reads go to the default filer (getEntry), not the key's owner filer.
weed/s3api/s3api_versioning_reconciler.g.if_broken: Stranded pointers persist until a client read heals them, so clients see spurious NoSuchKey.
weed/s3api/s3api_versioning_reconciler.g.ux: Rare NoSuchKey answers after interrupted version deletes disappear on their own within seconds.
weed/s3api/s3api_versioning_reconciler.g.what: versionsHealQueue is an in-memory map (capacity 4096) of bucket/key candidates, enqueued when a version delete removed the file but failed to update the pointer. runVersioningReconciler drains it every 5s; healVersionsPointer re-reads the .versions entry, probes the pointed-to file and, only when it is definitively missing, runs the same healStaleLatestVersionPointer the read path uses. Failures retry with exponential backoff (200ms to 30s, 6 attempts). Every log line carries '[versioning-heal] event=…' with sanitized fields for log aggregation.
weed/s3api/s3api_versioning_reconciler.g.when: Started with the server; candidates come from failed version deletes.
weed/s3api/s3api_versioning_reconciler.g.why: Consequence: a stranded pointer makes GET answer NoSuchKey for an object that still has older versions until someone reads it and the read path heals it. Design: healing proactively means idle keys and health checks see a consistent state. Transient errors are retried rather than treated as 'nothing to heal', so a filer blip cannot rewrite the pointer from an incomplete listing.

weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated.go.character: Go structs generated by xsdgen from AWS's S3 2006-03-01 XSD and since patched by hand. They are the XML wire shapes for listings, ACLs, copy results and versioning, plus the xsdDateTime type that fixes S3's timestamp format
gotchas: The header says 'Code generated by xsdgen. DO NOT EDIT.', but the file carries hand fixes: the value-receiver CopyObjectResult.MarshalXML, s3TimestampFormat, ListAllMyBucketsResult.ContinuationToken/Prefix, the pointer ListEntry.Owner (so Owner can be omitted), and Grantee moved out to s3api_xsd_generated_helper.go. Regenerating would silently undo all of them.

The other time-bearing types keep pointer-receiver MarshalXML. They get the S3 format only when the value is addressable (a slice element, or a field of something marshaled through a pointer); passing one by value, as CopyObjectResult once was, reverts to RFC 3339 with no error.
ListVersionsResult here has a single Version and DeleteMarker field, not a list; the real ListObjectVersions response uses its own type in s3api_object_versioning.go to avoid this one.
About half the file (Anon1–Anon30 and the SOAP envelopes) has no references; SeaweedFS does not serve the SOAP API.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated.go.if_broken: Every client that deserializes listings, ACLs or copy results breaks: wrong timestamps, missing Owner/StorageClass elements, or a namespace mismatch that makes strict parsers reject the whole document.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated.go.ux: Invisible when right. When wrong, SDKs fail to parse dates or elements (for example 'Text '...56Z' could not be parsed' in Java clients) on otherwise successful requests.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated.go.what: Holds the response types the handlers serialize. Those are ListBucketResult / ListEntry / PrefixEntry (wrapped by the V1/V2 listing types in s3api_object_handlers_list.go), VersionEntry and DeleteMarkerEntry (used by the ListObjectVersions builder in s3api_object_versioning.go), ListAllMyBucketsResult, AccessControlPolicy / AccessControlList / Grant / CanonicalUser, CopyObjectResult and VersioningConfiguration. Each struct with a time field gets a MarshalXML/UnmarshalXML pair that overlays the field with xsdDateTime, so it is written as UTC with exactly three fractional digits (s3TimestampFormat '2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z'); zero times are omitted. The rest of the file (Anon1–Anon30 and the SOAP request/response envelopes such as GetObjectExtended, PutObjectInline, SetBucketLoggingStatus) mirrors the XSD but is not referenced anywhere.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated.go.when: Whenever a listing, ListBuckets, Get*Acl, CopyObject / UploadPartCopy or GetBucketVersioning response is written; the Unmarshal side runs when request bodies such as AccessControlPolicy or VersioningConfiguration are parsed into these types.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated.go.why: Consequence: clients parse these documents with strict schemas, so a wrong element name, namespace or timestamp width breaks SDKs without any server-side error. Design: generating from the official XSD gave field names and namespaces that match AWS. The overlay pattern keeps plain time.Time fields for handler code while controlling the wire format in one place. AWS compatibility: the fixed three-digit fraction exists because minio-java parses LastModified with 'yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z''. CopyObjectResult.MarshalXML has a value receiver because handlers pass it by value, and encoding/xml ignores a pointer-receiver MarshalXML on a non-addressable value; it silently fell back to RFC 3339.

weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated_helper.go.character: The hand-written Grantee struct that the generated Grant type points at, taken out of the generated file so it can carry the xsi namespace attributes
gotchas: It is for output only. Incoming ACL bodies are parsed into aws-sdk-go's s3.Grantee (s3api_acl_helper.go), because the literal 'xsi:type,attr' tag does not match a namespaced attribute on decode.
The extra <Type> element is SeaweedFS-specific. Lenient clients ignore it, and a strict schema validator would reject it.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated_helper.go.if_broken: ACL responses lose the grantee type: clients show unknown grantees or fail to parse the grant list, and ACL round-trips (get, modify, put) break.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated_helper.go.ux: Lets aws-cli and the SDKs show grants with the right grantee type.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated_helper.go.what: Defines Grantee with XMLNS (written as the literal attribute 'xmlns:xsi'), XMLXSI (written as 'xsi:type'), and Type, ID, DisplayName and URI elements. buildAccessControlList (s3api_acl_helper.go) fills it with the XMLSchema-instance namespace and the grantee type when it renders GetBucketAcl / GetObjectAcl responses.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated_helper.go.when: Every ACL response (GetBucketAcl, GetObjectAcl) and any response that embeds an AccessControlList.
weed/s3api/s3api_xsd_generated_helper.go.why: Consequence: AWS ACL documents identify the grantee kind with xsi:type (CanonicalUser, Group, AmazonCustomerByEmail), and SDKs that dispatch on that attribute cannot read a grant without it. Design: Go's encoding/xml has no first-class support for prefixed attributes, so the attribute names are written literally in the struct tags. Keeping the type outside the generated file means regeneration cannot drop it. AWS compatibility: the output carries both the xsi:type attribute that AWS sends and a <Type> element that AWS does not.

weed/s3api/s3bucket/.character: The bucket-name validator shared by the gateway, weed shell, weed mini and the SQL filer stores
gotchas: auth_credentials.go wraps this with isASCIIBucketName because of the Unicode gap below, but only on its error-mapping path.
weed/s3api/s3bucket/.if_broken: Buckets with names that break DNS-style addressing or collide with filer internals can be created.
weed/s3api/s3bucket/.issue_note: The character test uses unicode.IsLower and unicode.IsNumber, which accept any Unicode lowercase letter or digit, while S3 allows only a-z, 0-9, '.' and '-'. auth_credentials.go documents this ('accept letters such as ü and digits such as ² that S3 refuses') and adds isASCIIBucketName, but CreateBucket (s3api_bucket_handlers.go:243) and the shell call VerifyS3BucketName alone, and path validation only rejects '/', '\' and NUL. So a bucket such as 'bücket' can be created, though it is unusable with virtual-host addressing and differs from AWS. Probe: VerifyS3BucketName returns nil for "bücket", "b²cket" and "ab٣".
weed/s3api/s3bucket/.ux: Invalid bucket names are refused with InvalidBucketName.
weed/s3api/s3bucket/.what: VerifyS3BucketName checks length 3–63, the reserved name 'filemeta', allowed characters (unicode.IsLower, unicode.IsNumber, '.', '-'), no adjacent periods, first and last character not '.' or '-', no 'xn--' prefix or '-s3alias' suffix, and not an IP address.
weed/s3api/s3bucket/.when: CreateBucket and other bucket-creating paths in the gateway, the error-code mapping in auth_credentials.go, weed shell bucket commands, weed mini's bucket bootstrap, and abstract_sql_store to decide whether a directory gets its own table.
weed/s3api/s3bucket/.why: Consequence: a bucket name becomes a filer directory, a collection name, a virtual-host DNS label and, on SQL filer stores, a per-bucket table name. 'filemeta' is reserved because a bucket with that name collides with the default filer table and cannot be deleted. Design: kept in a tiny package so the shell and the SQL store can use it without importing the gateway. AWS compatibility: follows the S3 general-purpose bucket naming rules.

weed/s3api/s3err/.character: Leaf package: S3 error codes (ErrorCode enum mapped to APIError{Code, Description, HTTPStatus}), the XML response writers, and the Fluent access/audit logger (a package-global Logger)
gotchas: Every new ErrorCode MUST get an errorCodeResponse entry: GetAPIError is a plain map lookup with no default, and a missing entry makes WriteHeader(0) panic.

getRemoteIP trusts X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP as-is for the audit log (unlike the policy engine, which honors only configured trusted proxies), so the logged remote_ip is client-spoofable unless the proxy strips these headers.
WriteResponse type-asserts w.(http.Flusher); a ResponseWriter wrapper that does not implement Flusher panics.
weed/s3api/s3err/.if_broken: Clients receive wrong statuses or malformed errors, so retries, 404 handling and conditional logic fail; or audit entries go missing or are duplicated.
weed/s3api/s3err/.issue_note: ErrMalformedCredentialDate (declared in the ErrorCode enum) has no entry in errorCodeResponse, so GetAPIError returns a zero APIError (status 0) and WriteErrorResponse panics with 'invalid WriteHeader code 0'. Reachable without credentials: any request whose SigV4 Authorization header (or presigned X-Amz-Credential, or POST-policy credential) carries a Credential date that does not parse returns this code from parseCredentialHeader (auth_signature_v4.go), and iam.Auth hands it straight to WriteErrorResponse before any key lookup. Reproduced at b9866bae with a throwaway test calling iam.Auth: the handler panics; under net/http the panic is recovered per connection, so the client sees a dropped connection instead of a 400 AuthorizationQueryParametersError. It is still the only ErrorCode without an entry at 917cf534.
weed/s3api/s3err/.ux: The exact XML error body, HTTP status and x-amz-request-id every client receives; the audit trail operators query.
weed/s3api/s3err/.what: Defines ~110 ErrorCode values and errorCodeResponse, the map to AWS error codes and HTTP statuses. WriteErrorResponse(WithMessage) builds the AWS RESTErrorResponse XML (Code, Message, Resource, RequestId, Key, BucketName), drains the request body for up to 30s, writes, and posts an audit entry. WriteXMLResponse/WriteAwsXMLResponse/WriteEmptyResponse/WriteResponse set x-amz-request-id and Accept-Ranges, apply fallback CORS headers on service-level requests, and suppress bodies for HEAD/1xx/204/304. audit_fluent.go builds AccessLog records (requester, principal ARN, OIDC claim, access key id, operation like REST.PUT.OBJECT, error code) and posts them asynchronously to Fluent, with a per-request flag so the track() middleware can emit a fallback entry without double-logging; WithAccessLogOperation lets a handler name the operation itself (S3 Vectors does), and bucket-level records without a key are logged too.
weed/s3api/s3err/.when: At the end of every request: errors from auth, the circuit breaker and handlers; success writers through s3api_handlers.go. InitAuditLog runs once when -auditLogConfig is set.
weed/s3api/s3err/.why: Consequence: every error any S3 client sees is shaped here; SDKs branch on the XML Code (NoSuchKey, SlowDown, PreconditionFailed…), so a wrong code or status breaks retries and existence checks. Design: the request body is drained on error so the client, which may still be streaming an upload, gets the error response instead of a connection reset. The audit 'already logged' flag lets handlers that log themselves coexist with the generic fallback. AWS compatibility: codes and statuses follow the AWS ErrorResponses table; several SeaweedFS-specific codes reuse AWS codes (InvalidArgument for bad directives).

weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/.character: The lifecycle engine's core vocabulary (top-level files only): the flat Rule, the compiled action kinds, evaluation and due-time math, and the hashes and shard function the worker keys its state on
gotchas: Expiration is measured from ModTime plus exact days, not rounded to the next midnight UTC as AWS does.
EvaluateAction and ComputeDueAt encode the same per-kind conditions in two switches; a change to one must be mirrored in the other.
tagPrefix in tags.go is declared but never used.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/.if_broken: Objects expire at the wrong time, the wrong versions are deleted, or worker state is invalidated on every run.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/.issue_note: version_time.go copies compareVersionIds, isNewFormatVersionId and getVersionTimestamp from weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go (its comment says so: 'kept duplicated to avoid the s3api -> s3lifecycle import cycle'). The lifecycle worker and the gateway must order version IDs identically, or noncurrent-version decisions diverge from what the gateway treats as latest. Moving the comparator into a leaf package both can import (for example s3_constants) would remove the copy.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/.ux: Lifecycle rules behave like AWS's, evaluated by a scheduled worker.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/.what: Rule and ObjectInfo describe a canonical rule and an object version. RuleActionKinds expands a rule into compiled kinds (expiration days/date, expired delete marker, noncurrent days or stand-alone newer-noncurrent, abort MPU). EvaluateAction decides whether a (rule, kind) fires for an object at a time. ComputeDueAt gives the earliest time it can fire. EventLogHorizon and MinTriggerAge give how far back the reader must replay and the safety-scan cadence. RuleHash (8 bytes of a length-prefixed sha256, stable across ID renames, status flips and tag order) and HashExtended (identity-CAS fingerprint) key persisted state; ShardID splits (bucket, key) into 16 shards. SuccessorFromEntryStamp reads the noncurrent-since stamp; CompareVersionIds orders version IDs. DaysToDuration scales days (10s per 'day' under the s3tests build tag). The subpackages (engine, reader, router, dispatcher, dailyrun, bootstrap) are outside this graph.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/.when: Used by the lifecycle worker, the scheduler, the gateway's LifecycleDelete endpoint (identity hash) and lifecycle_xml.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/.why: Consequence: these definitions decide which objects get deleted and when; a hash that changed across releases would make the worker re-walk everything, and an evaluation bug deletes data. Design: rules are compiled into (bucket, rule hash, kind) actions so each can be tracked, rate-limited and replayed independently from the filer meta log (see DESIGN.md: one daily pass that replays events per shard instead of long-running watchers). The identity hash lets the gateway refuse a delete whose target changed after scheduling. AWS compatibility: expiration, noncurrent-version, newer-noncurrent, expired-delete-marker and abort-MPU semantics follow S3 lifecycle.

weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/scheduler/.character: Loads every bucket's lifecycle configuration from the filer for the lifecycle scheduler, and owns the storage keys the gateway uses for that configuration
gotchas: AllActivePriorStates skips the bootstrap walk ('runs out-of-band of that flow for now'), so objects that predate the event-log horizon are not covered by this path.
Object Lock without a versioning flag still counts as versioned, matching how the gateway writes.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/scheduler/.if_broken: Lifecycle stops for some or all buckets, or versioned buckets are treated as unversioned and lose history.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/scheduler/.ux: Lifecycle rules set through the S3 API are picked up by the next scheduled run.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/scheduler/.what: Declares BucketLifecycleConfigurationXMLKey, BucketLifecycleTransitionMinimumObjectSizeKey and the 1 MiB MaxBucketLifecycleConfigurationSize (the gateway aliases them). LoadCompileInputs pages through the buckets directory (1024 per page), parses each bucket's stored lifecycle XML with lifecycle_xml.ParseCanonical, and returns engine.CompileInput values, collecting parse failures as ParseError instead of dropping them. IsBucketVersioned treats Enabled, Suspended or Object Lock as versioned. AllActivePriorStates marks every compiled action as bootstrap-complete and event-driven.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/scheduler/.when: Each scheduler run, and the gateway's lifecycle configuration storage (s3api_bucket_lifecycle_config.go) through the aliased constants.
weed/s3api/s3lifecycle/scheduler/.why: Consequence: a bucket whose configuration is skipped never expires anything, silently. Design: the keys live here so the gateway, the admin dashboard and the scheduler share one definition without importing the gateway; malformed configurations are reported so operators can see them.

weed/s3api/s3tables/.character: The S3 Tables catalog as a package of its own: about 40 JSON operations over table buckets, namespaces, tables and views, stored as filer directories whose extended attributes are the catalog records. It has its own policy evaluator and a claim-and-compare protocol that keeps concurrent creates, deletes and renames consistent without a lock service
gotchas: Only CreateTableBucket consults the advanced-IAM authorizer (shouldUseIAM / authorizeIAMAction). Every other operation decides by owner, legacy identity Actions and the resource policies, so an IAM or STS policy that grants s3tables:* does not by itself open another principal's bucket.

Principals come from the identity by reflection (aws:userid > sub > preferred_username, then Account.Id or the identity name), and normalizePrincipalID collapses an ARN to its trailing name, so user/alice in two accounts is the same owner.

Resource-policy conditions only see s3tables:* keys, tags and aws:TagKeys. Global keys such as aws:SourceIp are never supplied, so a Deny on IpAddress never matches and a Deny on NotIpAddress matches everyone.

CreateTable (and CreateView) on an existing name of the same format answers 200 with the existing table's token and location and ignores the request's metadata; AWS answers Conflict. The Iceberg REST CreateTable turns that into 409, its CreateView does not (see iceberg/handlers_view.go).

ValidateTags exists but no HTTP handler of this package calls it (only weed shell, the admin console and s3vectors do). CreateTableBucket, CreateTable and TagResource on the S3 Tables API accept any number of tags with any characters. TagResource/UntagResource merge the request into the tags the record holds at the compare-checked write (updateTags), so concurrent tag writes do not drop each other; an in-process caller can cap the result with WithMaxTags, which s3vectors does.
Denied UpdateView / DeleteView answer 403, while the table operations keep the 404 existence veil unless the caller can read the entry.
ValidateTableBucketUpload treats every path under /buckets/ as a table bucket path; callers must check isTableBucket first.
CreateNamespace logs every permission check at glog.Infof (not V-gated).

A table created under a renamed table's old name keeps its record entry on that directory while its files go to <name>-<uuid>; DeleteTable of the renamed table is then refused ('location in use'), and deleting the new table leaves the renamed table's files.
CatalogRecordRoots lists every namespace and record of the bucket, so creates, registers, renames and root-moving updates cost a scan of the whole catalog of that bucket.
weed/s3api/s3tables/.if_broken: Tables disappear or appear twice, a drop deletes another table's data or leaves orphaned files, Iceberg commits are lost to concurrent writers, or policy evaluation opens a bucket to principals it should exclude.
weed/s3api/s3tables/.issue_note: CreateTable and CreateView can wipe a record another create just registered. Both make the record directory with ensureDirectory, a lookup followed by a non-exclusive CreateEntry, and the filer answers a non-exclusive directory create over an existing directory by replacing the entry, extended attributes included. A create whose lookup misses and whose CreateEntry lands after a second creator has finished therefore clears that creator's record and claims the empty entry: both answer 200, the catalog holds the later table, and the first table (with any commit it already took) is gone from the catalog while its files stay behind. createDirectoryExclusive and retakeDirectory in filer_ops.go already give the exclusive behaviour; the record path does not use them. Probe at b9866bae (Iceberg REST over the MemFiler, CreateEntry hook): B creates ns.orders and commits v2 between A's lookup and A's CreateEntry; A and B both get 200 and LoadTable serves A's empty table. The window is narrow, since B must finish between two of A's calls. The code is unchanged at 917cf534. Three earlier defects of this package are fixed upstream: a table renamed across namespaces can commit again (#12515), RenameTable refuses a source that changed between its reads (#12446), and policy Condition blocks are validated and fail safe (#12389).
weed/s3api/s3tables/.ux: aws s3tables commands, Spark/Trino/PyIceberg via the Iceberg REST endpoint, and the admin UI all see one catalog. Races answer 409 Conflict ('changed during …, retry the request') instead of corrupting state, and denials usually look like NoSuchTable/NoSuchBucket.
weed/s3api/s3tables/.what: S3TablesHandler.HandleRequest dispatches on X-Amz-Target to the handlers for buckets, namespaces, tables (CreateTable, RegisterTable, Get/List/Update/Delete, RenameTable), views, table and bucket policies, maintenance configuration and job status, and tags. A table bucket is /buckets/<name> marked s3tables.tableBucket; a namespace is /buckets/<bucket>/<ns> and a table or view is /buckets/<bucket>/<ns>/<name>, each with JSON metadata, policy, tags and maintenance in s3tables.* xattrs. filer_ops.go writes every record compare-and-swap (UpdateEntry with ExpectedExtended, a snapshot that also asserts the package's absent keys, retried 5 times). In-flight operations mark records through ExtendedKeyDeleting: 'create' and 'rename-dest' hide a record until its parent is re-checked (confirmParent), and a random token claims a bucket or namespace for delete. Deletes remove only what is still exactly as scanned (deleteDirectoryIfMatches, removeEmptyTree). Each record owns the directory its files live in (CatalogRecordRoot: the metadata location's table directory inside the bucket, else the WarehouseLocation a create without a location assigns as <name>-<uuid>, else the record path; a renamed record keeps the directory of its old name). CatalogRecordRoots maps every record of the bucket to those roots, plus the target of a move in progress (ExtendedKeyMoving), and create, register, view create, rename destination and root-moving updates refuse a root another record's entry or files overlap (claimCatalogEntryAt, moveCatalogRecord). UpdateTable/UpdateView check a new location after authorization: inside the record's namespace, or in the directory it already holds and no other record keeps files in. RenameTable has a REST route, compares the metadata it copies with the snapshot it claimed, and checks the version token against that snapshot. permissions.go evaluates its own PolicyDocument. The owner is always allowed. Identity Actions grant s3tables:<Op>[:<bucket>] with wildcards and admin markers. A Deny in the table or bucket policy vetoes both. Conditions see s3tables:* keys, request/resource/bucket tags (s3vectors:VectorBucketTag/<key> reads the bucket tags too) and aws:TagKeys; a policy is refused at store time when a condition is null, split, keyless or has values its operator cannot read (ConditionValue), and an unusable stored condition fails safe (a Deny applies, an Allow never grants). Manager runs the same handlers in-process through httptest for weed shell, the admin console, the Iceberg and Lance REST catalogs and S3 Vectors; in-process callers can bind bucket-scoped operations (CreateNamespace, DeleteNamespace, CreateTable, DeleteTable, DeleteTableBucket, the tag operations) to the bucket they authorized with WithTableBucketCreatedAt, and cap tag counts with WithMaxTags; it also offers AuthorizeCreateTable / AuthorizeUpdateTable for credential vending and permission checks. DeclaredEncryption tells S3 Vectors whether a bucket declares SSE-S3. The package also holds the Iceberg upload-layout validator (metadata/, data/, Lance '_' dirs) and manifest / manifest-list readers that repair iceberg-go partition and format-version quirks.
weed/s3api/s3tables/.when: Every S3 Tables request on the S3 port (s3api_tables.go routes JSON X-Amz-Target and REST paths through authenticateS3Tables, which authenticates only). Every Iceberg REST catalog call (weed/s3api/iceberg) through Manager.Execute, and weed shell / admin console table commands through a trusted Manager. The layout validator runs on S3 uploads into table buckets.
weed/s3api/s3tables/.why: Consequence: this catalog decides which Iceberg or Lance table a name resolves to and where its data lives, so a lost race either strands data or lets a delete purge a directory another table still points at. Design: the filer has no multi-key transactions, so every operation is a sequence of compare-checked single-entry writes plus claims that a competing operation must respect. That is why creates write a hidden record and confirm the parent afterwards, deletes claim before they scan, and a root is claimed and then checked again with the record written, so of two creates racing for one directory at least one backs out (#12473). Tables created without a location get a directory of their own so a later table of the same name cannot inherit, or purge, a renamed table's files (#12475). Authorization veils existence: a caller who may not read a resource gets the same 404 as for a missing one (authorizeAbsentTarget, canReadEntry), and location checks run after authorization so they reveal nothing either. Rename is catalog-only because Iceberg manifests embed absolute paths, so the data stays and the destination keeps the old MetadataLocation, which later commits may keep writing to (#12515). Policies with unusable conditions are refused instead of being evaluated as if the condition were absent (#12389). AWS compatibility: the operation names, JSON shapes, ARN formats (any partition), name rules, reserved prefixes and the AES256-only encryption mirror AWS S3 Tables. UpdateNamespace, views, RegisterTable, LANCE buckets and the Format field are SeaweedFS extensions for the Iceberg REST catalog and the vector store.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/execute.go.character: In-process entry point for trusted local tooling (the admin console): runs one S3 Vectors operation as a named identity without signing
gotchas: The AST shows no in-package caller; its callers live in weed/admin, outside this graph.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/execute.go.if_broken: Admin console vector operations fail or bypass checks.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/execute.go.ux: The admin UI shows and edits vector buckets with the same rules as the API.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/execute.go.what: Execute looks up the operation's handler, marshals the request into an httptest request carrying only the identity name, runs the handler and decodes the response or returns an Error{Code, Message} for status >= 400.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/execute.go.when: Admin console vector bucket and index pages (weed/admin/dash/s3vectors_management.go).
weed/s3api/s3vectors/execute.go.why: Consequence: the admin console manages vector buckets through this; it must reach exactly the same code path as the API. Design: mirrors s3tables.Manager.Execute: nothing is authenticated, and the identity's grants decide what the operation may do.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/handlers.go.character: The S3 Vectors operations: vector buckets (s3tables table buckets of format LANCE), bucket policies with their own evaluator, indexes (catalog entries in the implicit 'vector' namespace) and vector reads, writes and queries forwarded to the VectorService engine
gotchas: A vector bucket whose s3tables policy contains s3vectors statements is governed by that policy until a vector policy is put; PutVectorBucketPolicy then strips those statements.
authorizeVectorTags reads the bucket record and its policy in two separate lookups.

An index whose engine create had an unknown outcome stays in the catalog marked initializing; GetIndex and ListIndexes do not hide it, and only a CreateIndex with the same dimension, metric and non-filterable keys clears it.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/handlers.go.if_broken: Vector writes or queries fail, indexes report wrong dimensions, or policies grant the wrong principals.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/handlers.go.ux: Applications store embeddings and run similarity search through the AWS S3 Vectors SDK.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/handlers.go.what: The dispatch table maps every operation name to a handler. Buckets: CreateVectorBucket checks s3vectors:CreateVectorBucket (and TagResource for tags) against the handler account, through the IAM authorizer when the gateway has one, and creates a LANCE table bucket; Get/List filter on the vector policy; Delete drops the implicit index namespace when it is the only content, bound to the authorized bucket. Policies: validateVectorPolicy accepts only s3vectors actions and resources and tag condition keys, refuses misspelled Statement/Effect/Condition keys, a null Allow condition, a condition split over several keys, an operator with no key, and values the operator cannot read (s3tables.ConditionValue); Put/Delete rewrite the vector policy xattr with a compare-checked write that also strips s3vectors statements from the s3tables policy. authorizeVectorTags evaluates the action against the vector policy with bucket, index and request tags. Indexes: CreateIndex authorizes, ensures the implicit namespace, writes the catalog record first marked initializing (dimension, metric, non-filterable keys, a createNonce), re-reads it to confirm its own nonce and version token won, creates the engine index, then clears the mark. An initializing record with the same parameters is resumed instead of refused; on a definite engine failure the record is deleted only if nonce and token still match, while an unknown outcome leaves it. Vectors: Put validates dimension and batch size; Get/List/Delete forward to the engine; List emulates segments when the engine cannot; Query checks dimension and non-filterable keys, translates the JSON filter into a SQL expression over json_extract(metadata, ...) and converts squared L2 distances to euclidean. Every authorization records the bucket and index for metrics and the access log.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/handlers.go.why: Consequence: this is the whole vector store API; a wrong authorization opens a bucket's vectors to other principals, and a wrong index record makes every write fail on dimension. Design: the catalog owns names, policies and tags, the engine owns vector data, and every write that spans both puts the catalog record first and rolls back only what this request provably created (nonce plus version token), and only when the engine definitely refused: an Unavailable or other unknown outcome may already have created the engine index. The initializing mark lets a retry of the same request finish instead of hitting 409. The vector policy is a separate document so s3vectors grants never leak into S3 Tables evaluation. Compatibility: operation names, limits (500 per put, 100 keys per get, topK 10000, 16 segments), distance metrics and the filter operators ($eq, $ne, $in, $nin, $exists, $and, $or, ranges) follow AWS S3 Vectors.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/server.go.character: The S3 Vectors HTTP surface: one handler that dispatches every operation by X-Amz-Target or by path, wrapped in SigV4 authentication and per-operation metrics
gotchas: Authentication failures all answer 403 AccessDenied, including malformed signatures.
A request without Content-Length reserves the full maximum body size from the byte budget while it waits and runs.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/server.go.if_broken: Every S3 Vectors call fails, or metrics stop reporting.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/server.go.ux: boto3 / aws s3vectors commands work against SeaweedFS; vector buckets show up in the gateway's per-bucket metrics and access log.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/server.go.what: Server holds a filer client, two s3tables Managers (one that authorizes as the caller, one trusted for bookkeeping such as format lookups and the implicit index namespace), the VectorService client (the discovery client, wrapped by SetDescribe), the authenticator, the region and account id embedded in the ARNs it mints, an optional limiter and two semaphores. RegisterRoutes mounts POST / (operation from X-Amz-Target), POST /{op} and GET/POST/DELETE /tags/{resourceArn}. instrument labels the request with its operation, records in-flight count, latency, status, per-bucket traffic and active time (only for a bucket the request was authorized on) and posts one access-log entry. Auth rejects bodies over S3VectorsMaxRequestBodyBytes, takes a request slot and a share of the byte budget before reading anything (408 RequestTimeout when the wait is cancelled), bounds the body in the context, authenticates with the gateway's S3 authenticator (failure answers 403 AccessDenied) and puts the identity in the context. dispatch hands the request to limitRequest when a limiter is set.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/server.go.when: Process start (command/s3.go wires it with the discovered vector engine, the Lance describe and the gateway's limiter and upload limits) and every S3 Vectors request.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/server.go.why: Consequence: every S3 Vectors call enters here; a dispatch mismatch makes SDK calls fail with 'unknown operation', and unbounded concurrent bodies can exhaust the gateway's memory before authentication. Design: one dispatch table (handlers.go) serves both the JSON-target and the per-path styles AWS SDKs use; the trusted Manager exists because bookkeeping that accompanies an already-authorized operation must not demand catalog read grants the S3 Vectors API does not require. The slot and byte semaphores bound buffering before authentication (#12537); metrics are labelled with the bucket only once authorization named it, so an unauthenticated caller cannot create label series. Compatibility: the request styles, the tagging paths and the ARN form arn:aws:s3vectors:<region>:<account>:bucket/<name>[/index/<name>] follow AWS S3 Vectors.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/tagging.go.character: TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource for vector buckets and indexes, stored as s3tables tags
gotchas: UntagResource validates the keys only after authorization, so a denied caller gets AccessDenied rather than a validation error.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/tagging.go.if_broken: Tag-based access control acts on wrong tags, or tags land on another bucket.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/tagging.go.ux: aws s3vectors tag-resource / untag-resource / list-tags-for-resource work.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/tagging.go.what: tagTarget resolves the resourceArn (from the /tags/ path or the body) to bucket and optional index and to the catalog ARN the record is keyed by. authorizeTagging checks the s3vectors action against the vector bucket policy (with request tags for TagResource), binds the catalog calls to the authorized bucket's creation time, and requires an index target to be a LANCE-format entry. TagResource validates at most 50 tags and passes WithMaxTags(50) so the merged total is capped at the compare-checked write. Untag validates each key; List returns the stored tags.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/tagging.go.when: Tagging calls on vector buckets and indexes.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/tagging.go.why: Consequence: tags drive tag-conditioned vector bucket policies (aws:ResourceTag, s3vectors:VectorBucketTag), so a tag write can grant or revoke access. Design: tags live in the s3tables records, merged inside the catalog's compare, so concurrent tag writes do not drop each other; the bucket binding keeps a write from landing on a bucket created again under the same name. Compatibility: the 50-tag limit and path forms follow AWS S3 Vectors.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/types.go.character: S3 Vectors wire types plus the JSON/error writers and the bounded body reader
gotchas: readJSON caches the body on the request info: a handler that reads r.Body directly after the limiter decoded it gets the replayed copy, not the stream.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/types.go.if_broken: SDKs fail to parse responses or errors.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/types.go.ux: SDK calls decode responses without errors.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/types.go.what: Request and response structs for vector buckets, bucket policies, indexes, vectors (put, get, list with segments, delete, query) and tagging. writeJSON answers application/x-amz-json-1.1 with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; writeError answers {__type, code, message, requestId}. readJSON reads at most the body limit, rejects larger bodies, and keeps the bytes in the request's info so the limiter and the handler decode one read.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/types.go.why: Consequence: AWS SDKs parse these shapes; a renamed field breaks every client. Design: the error carries both __type and code because SDKs read one or the other. Compatibility: field names and limits follow the AWS S3 Vectors API.

weed/s3api/stats.go.character: The outermost per-route middleware (track) plus the per-bucket traffic and latency counters handlers call directly
gotchas: The V(2) access log uses %q so requester- and key-supplied bytes (newlines) cannot forge extra log lines.
Metric cardinality still grows with the number of real buckets, since every authorized request is labelled by bucket.
weed/s3api/stats.go.if_broken: Missing metrics or audit entries; a panic here would fail every request.
weed/s3api/stats.go.ux: Operators get per-action and per-bucket request rates, latencies, bytes and an audit entry per request; clients see the Server header.
weed/s3api/stats.go.what: track wraps every S3 route. It increments the in-flight gauge for the action, sets the 'Server: SeaweedFS <version>' header, attaches an audit-tracking flag and a mutable identity holder to the request, times the handler through a status-recording writer, logs the request at V(2), records the request histogram and counter labelled by action, status and bucket, marks the bucket active, and emits a fallback audit entry (PostLog) for handlers that did not log one themselves. TimeToFirstByte, BucketTrafficReceived and BucketTrafficSent record per-bucket latency and byte counters from inside handlers.
weed/s3api/stats.go.when: Every routed S3 request (registerRouter wraps each handler as track(iam.Auth(cb.Limit(...)))); the traffic helpers on object reads and writes.
weed/s3api/stats.go.why: Consequence: these are the Prometheus metrics and audit log operators rely on; a handler path that skips them is invisible in dashboards and the audit trail. Design: track sits outside iam.Auth, so the identity holder is attached before authentication, which lets the fallback audit entry name the requester even though auth stores the identity on a request copy track never sees. The bucket label is dropped on 403s so unauthenticated probes for random bucket names cannot grow metric cardinality.

weed/s3api/tags.go.character: The S3 Tagging XML types and the parsers and validators shared by object and bucket tagging
gotchas: Object tag validation lives in the s3tables package (s3tables.ValidateTagsWithLimit), so changing the S3 Tables tag rules changes object tagging too.
A key with no '=' is stored with an empty value, as AWS does.
weed/s3api/tags.go.if_broken: Tag-based policies and lifecycle rules see different tags than were stored, or invalid tags are accepted and break later reads.
weed/s3api/tags.go.ux: aws s3api put-object-tagging and --tagging behave as on AWS; invalid tags fail with InvalidTag instead of being stored.
weed/s3api/tags.go.what: Defines Tag / TagSet / Tagging (the XML body of Put/GetObjectTagging and Put/GetBucketTagging) with ToTags and FromTags (sorted by key for stable output). parseTagsHeader decodes the x-amz-tagging header (URL-query style, empty segments skipped, duplicate keys rejected). ValidateTags (10 tags, for objects) and ValidateBucketTags (50) delegate to the s3tables tag validator: key 1–128 runes, value up to 256, a restricted Unicode character set.
weed/s3api/tags.go.when: PutObject / CopyObject / CreateMultipartUpload with x-amz-tagging, the object and bucket tagging handlers, and policy rechecks that read stored tags.
weed/s3api/tags.go.why: Consequence: tags feed bucket-policy conditions (s3:ExistingObjectTag, s3:RequestObjectTag) and lifecycle filters, so a parser that disagrees with the policy engine authorizes one tag set and stores another. Design: parseTagsHeader skips empty segments exactly as url.ParseQuery does, so CopyObject stores the same keys that PutObject and bucket policies see. AWS compatibility: the limits and character set follow AWS (10 per object, 50 per bucket).

weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/.character: The Iceberg maintenance plugin worker, collapsed to one node: it scans table buckets for tables that need work and rewrites their files and metadata directly on the filer — data compaction, position-delete rewrite, snapshot expiry, orphan removal and manifest rewriting
gotchas: Detection reads raw table entries, so records an s3tables operation has hidden (an unfinished create) or claimed (a delete or rename in progress) are proposed and processed like any other.
updateTableMetadataXattr, persistPlanningIndex and recordJobStatus never check ExtendedKeyDeleting, so they write records that a rename or delete has claimed (see issue note).
A commit that fails for any reason other than a version conflict deletes the metadata file it just wrote, even if the record update may have applied.
The node is collapsed: compaction, delete rewrite, row lineage and geometry handling live in ~20 files not drawn individually.
weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/.if_broken: Small files and snapshots accumulate, storage is not reclaimed, or a maintenance commit corrupts a table or wedges it for catalog writers.
weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/.issue_note: The worker ignores the s3tables claim protocol. Its record writes (updateTableMetadataXattr in filer_io.go, persistPlanningIndex, recordJobStatus) assert the attribute snapshot they read, which includes an ExtendedKeyDeleting marker if one is present, so they succeed on a record that a RenameTable or DeleteTable has claimed. Probe (s3tablestest MemFiler, worker-style write with the same checks as filer_io.go): a maintenance commit landing between a rename's claim and its source clear makes the rename fail ('table changed during rename') and its release fail too, leaving the source marked Deleting=rename; afterwards UpdateTable answers 409 'table was updated concurrently' and DeleteTable 'table changed during delete' until the same rename is retried. Re-probed at b9866bae, after #12446: still reproduced. A worker-style commit after the rename's claim succeeds, the rename answers 409 and the source stays marked Deleting=rename, after which UpdateTable and DeleteTable answer 409. Re-checked at 917cf534: the worker still reads and writes no claim marker (no reference to ExtendedKeyDeleting or ExtendedKeyMoving under weed/worker/tasks/iceberg); the shared-location skip added in #12473 does not touch this path.
weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/.ux: Tables stay fast to scan and their storage shrinks after expiry; job status shows in the admin UI and through GetTableMaintenanceJobStatus.
weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/.what: handler.go registers the 'iceberg_maintenance' job type with the plugin worker framework. Detect (detection.go) walks table buckets and namespaces (bucket/namespace/table wildcard filters, resource-group fairness), reads each table entry's s3tables metadata xattr, skips non-Iceberg entries and decides from snapshot, manifest and small-file thresholds (cached in a planning index stored in the record) which tables get a proposal. A table whose files another catalog record also points at, above, at or under its location (s3tables.CatalogRecordRoots and PathsOverlap; a record sitting only on the root, as one created over a renamed table's old name does, does not count), is never proposed, and remove_orphans re-checks this when it runs, because those operations delete what this table's metadata does not reference (#12473). Execute dials the filer, loads the table's maintenance configuration and current metadata, merges table properties over the worker config (table_config.go) and runs the requested operations in order: compact (compact*.go, schema_evolution.go, sort_strategy.go, row_lineage.go, geometry_*.go: bin-pack small Parquet files per partition and spec), rewrite_position_delete_files (delete_rewrite.go, eqdelete_scope.go), expire_snapshots, remove_orphans (files under metadata/ and data/ that no snapshot, metadata-log entry or statistics file references and that are older than orphan_older_than_hours, default 72) and rewrite_manifests. Each operation commits through commitWithRetry: build the new metadata with iceberg-go, write v{N+1}-<nanos>.metadata.json, then updateTableMetadataXattr (filer_io.go) rewrites the record's metadata and metadataVersion xattrs with a conditional UpdateEntry whose precondition is the whole attribute snapshot; a conflict deletes the file and retries with exponential backoff. recordJobStatus (job_status.go) and persistPlanningIndex (planning_index.go) write the record the same way.
weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/.when: Periodically, when the admin server schedules iceberg_maintenance detection and assigns proposals to plugin workers.
weed/worker/tasks/iceberg/.why: Consequence: without maintenance, streaming writers leave thousands of small files and an ever-growing snapshot history, so scans slow down and storage is never reclaimed; a wrong commit here rewrites a table under its writers. Design: the worker bypasses the S3 Tables and Iceberg REST layers and writes the filer directly, using the record's attribute snapshot as the compare-and-swap, so a concurrent catalog commit makes the maintenance commit fail and retry instead of being overwritten. Orphan removal uses an age threshold rather than proving files unreferenced at one instant, the same safety window Iceberg's own orphan removal uses.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/describe.go.character: The bridge that fills in where a vector index lives before a request reaches the engine
weed/s3api/s3vectors/describe.go.what: SetDescribe wraps the VectorService client in describedClient. For each engine call (CreateIndex, DropIndex, Put/Get/Delete/List/QueryVectors) whose table has an id but no location, it resolves the id through the injected DescribeFn (the Lance catalog's in-process DescribeTableInternal) and sets Location, and sets SseS3 when the vector bucket declares AES256 encryption. describeErr maps catalog errors to the gRPC codes the engine itself would answer: NoSuchTable/Namespace/Bucket to NotFound, AccessDenied to PermissionDenied, anything else to Internal.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/describe.go.why: Consequence: the engine opens the Lance dataset by location, so without this every engine call would need its own catalog round trip, and an engine that missed the encryption flag would write the bucket's files unencrypted while the S3 path encrypts them. Design: resolution happens in the gateway, in process, with the already-authorized request, so no unauthenticated HTTP call to the Lance catalog is needed and the engine never needs catalog credentials. Mapping to gRPC codes lets vectorErr translate catalog and engine failures the same way.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/describe.go.when: Wired once at startup by command/s3.go and the s3vectors shell command; runs on every S3 Vectors call that reaches the engine.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/describe.go.ux: Vector operations reach the right dataset; a missing index answers NotFound like the engine would.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/describe.go.if_broken: Engine calls fail or open the wrong dataset, or encrypted vector buckets get unencrypted index files.
gotchas: A table that already carries a Location is passed through unresolved, so the caller-supplied location is trusted.
The encryption flag is read with a second catalog lookup per call.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/discovery.go.character: The client-side load balancer to the vector engine: finds a weed-vector process through the masters and fails over between them
weed/s3api/s3vectors/discovery.go.what: NewVectorDiscovery returns a VectorService client whose every call first gets a connection from cli. cli starts an asynchronous resolve when due (every 5 s while connected, every 0.5 s while not), waits for it only when there is no client yet, and counts the call against the client so a replaced connection closes only after its last call. resolve asks the masters' ListClusterNodes for 'vector' nodes of the filer group, skips a follower that answers empty, prefers the current worker, avoids the one that last failed, and dials a new one when it changes. Each call is tried twice: an Unavailable error resets the connection (marking that worker failed) and retries once; other errors return at once. CreateIndex returns the first attempt's error when the retry also fails, so an unknown first outcome is not reported as a definite refusal.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/discovery.go.why: Consequence: without it the gateway would need a fixed engine address and every engine restart would fail vector calls until reconfigured. Design: discovery goes through the master registry the engines register with, so engines can move or scale; the retry is limited to transport failures, and CreateIndex keeps its first error because the index handler rolls back its catalog record only on a definite engine refusal.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/discovery.go.when: Built once at startup (command/s3.go, and the s3vectors shell command); every S3 Vectors call that reaches the engine.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/discovery.go.ux: Vector calls keep working across a weed-vector restart, after at most one failed attempt.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/discovery.go.if_broken: Every vector call fails with 'no weed-vector registered on master', or calls stick to a dead engine.
gotchas: Every successful lookup logs each discovered worker at glog level 0, so a busy gateway logs the engine addresses every few seconds.
Only the first worker that is not the failed one is used; there is no spreading of load across several engines.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/iam.go.character: The hook that lets the gateway's IAM policies take part in S3 Vectors authorization
weed/s3api/s3vectors/iam.go.what: checkPermission first asks the authenticator, when it implements IAMAuthorizer, to evaluate the action on the resource: an explicit IAM deny refuses, an IAM allow adds the action to the identity's actions for this check. It then runs the S3 Tables evaluator (owner, identity actions, resource policy with conditions).
weed/s3api/s3vectors/iam.go.why: Consequence: without it, an IAM user or STS role granted s3vectors:* by an attached policy would still be refused unless the resource policy also named it, and an IAM deny would be ignored. Design: IAM is folded in as an extra identity action, so the resource-policy rules (and their own denies) still apply on top; the IAM evaluator receives the same policy context, so tag conditions work in IAM policies too.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/iam.go.when: Every bucket, index, vector and tagging authorization in handlers.go.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/iam.go.ux: S3 Vectors permissions can be granted through IAM policies as on AWS.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/iam.go.if_broken: IAM-granted callers are refused, or IAM denies stop applying to vector buckets.
gotchas: With no IAM authorizer (static identities only) the check is the S3 Tables evaluator alone.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/limits.go.character: Admission control for S3 Vectors: per-bucket rate limits from the gateway and process-wide concurrency and byte budgets
weed/s3api/s3vectors/limits.go.what: SetRequestLimits creates the slot semaphore (default 16 concurrent requests) and the byte semaphore (default 8 x the maximum body) that Auth takes from. SetLimiter installs the gateway's limiter. limitRequest decodes just enough of the request to name its target (tag ARN, bucket name or ARN, index name or ARN), records the target, maps the operation to the gateway's read or write action (Get*, List*, QueryVectors read; everything else write), sets mux vars bucket/object so the gateway's per-bucket limits apply, and runs the handler through the limiter. A request the limiter refuses gets its XML error converted to the S3 Vectors JSON error (ThrottlingException by default).
weed/s3api/s3vectors/limits.go.why: Consequence: S3 Vectors runs beside the S3 API on the same gateway and must obey the same per-bucket limits (#12514), or vector traffic could starve object traffic and dodge configured quotas. Design: the limiter speaks S3 (XML, bucket/object vars), so the request is translated in and the refusal translated back; the body is decoded once and replayed to the handler.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/limits.go.when: Every S3 Vectors request when command/s3.go set a limiter (it always does), after authentication and before the handler.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/limits.go.ux: Throttled vector calls get ThrottlingException like on AWS; operators configure one set of limits for both APIs.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/limits.go.if_broken: Vector calls bypass bucket limits, or every vector call is refused with a mistranslated error.
gotchas: A request whose target cannot be resolved answers 400 ValidationException before reaching the handler, so the handler's own validation message is not the one the client sees.
The index name is passed to the gateway limiter as the object key, so object-key based limit rules also match index names.

weed/s3api/s3vectors/operations.go.character: The sorted list of S3 Vectors operation names
weed/s3api/s3vectors/operations.go.what: Operations returns the keys of the dispatch table, sorted.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/operations.go.why: Consequence: the admin console's policy-action suggestions and the s3vectors shell command validate names against it, so a new handler shows up in both without editing either. Design: derived from the dispatch table instead of a second list that could drift.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/operations.go.when: Admin console policy editor and the weed shell s3vectors command.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/operations.go.ux: Operators see every supported s3vectors action when writing policies.
weed/s3api/s3vectors/operations.go.if_broken: The shell refuses valid operations or the console suggests missing ones.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list_pr.character: Read-ahead for recursive listings: keeps several directory reads in flight in the order the listing walk will enter them
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list_pr.what: listPrefetcher queues every directory the walk will descend into (not .uploads or .versions), kept in '<path>/' byte order, and up to 8 workers read the first window of each (at most 32 entries or max-keys+2, and at most 128 KiB). take hands the walk the window for the directory it is entering, drops windows for directories the walk has passed, and tells the walk whether the window ended the directory; the walk reads the rest itself. The number of windows held or in flight starts at the worker count and doubles up to 64 (bounded by max-keys) while directories keep ending inside their first window, and falls back when one does not. list runs the walk's own listing of a directory through a reader that queues its child directories as they arrive, buffering at most 1 MiB ahead. close cancels every read and waits for them.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list_pr.why: Consequence: a recursive listing (no '/' delimiter) of a tree of many small directories was one filer round trip per directory, in series, which made large listings slow (#12438). Design: prefetching follows the walk's byte order, so the windows read are the ones the walk will need next; the adaptive cap keeps a page that ends inside a large directory from leaving many windows unread, and waiting for all readers in close keeps none outliving the filer client.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list_pr.when: ListObjects V1/V2 without the '/' delimiter (aws s3 ls --recursive, sync tools, Hadoop-style recursive listings).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list_pr.ux: Recursive listings of deep or branched prefixes return faster.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_list_pr.if_broken: Recursive listings skip or duplicate keys (a window handed to the wrong directory or misjudged as complete), hang, or leak filer streams.
gotchas: A window is only used when the walk's request has no prefix and no start position; otherwise the walk lists the directory itself.
At most 4096 directories are queued; further ones are listed when the walk reaches them.

weed/s3api/s3api_vector_iam.go.character: The gateway's side of S3 Vectors authorization: evaluates the caller's IAM policies for an s3vectors action
weed/s3api/s3api_vector_iam.go.what: EvaluateIAMPolicy implements s3vectors.IAMAuthorizer. It turns the vector policy context into condition keys (aws:ResourceTag/*, s3vectors:VectorBucketTag/*, aws:RequestTag/*, aws:TagKeys) carried in the request context, evaluates the identity's attached IAM policies, and reports denied on an attached or explicit IAM deny. For an identity routed through the IAM integration (STS sessions, identities without static actions, identities with attached policies) it asks VerifyActionPermission; a session that is not allowed is reported as denied. Otherwise it reports allowed when an attached policy allows.
weed/s3api/s3api_vector_iam.go.why: Consequence: without it the S3 Vectors API ignored IAM policies, so users and roles granted s3vectors actions by IAM could not use vector buckets, and IAM denies did not apply. Design: the condition keys are passed through the context so the existing IAM evaluators (auth_credentials.go, s3_iam_middleware.go) see the vector tags without a new interface; the STS rule makes a session's role policy a ceiling, as for the S3 API.
weed/s3api/s3api_vector_iam.go.when: Every S3 Vectors authorization (through s3vectors/iam.go checkPermission).
weed/s3api/s3api_vector_iam.go.ux: IAM users and STS roles get S3 Vectors permissions from their policies.
weed/s3api/s3api_vector_iam.go.if_broken: IAM-granted callers are refused vector operations, or IAM denies are ignored.
gotchas: For an STS session, an action its policies do not allow is a deny, so a vector bucket policy cannot grant the session more than its role allows.

weed/pb/filer.proto.character: The filer's wire contract: the SeaweedFiler gRPC service and every message the gateway, mounts, shell and peer filers exchange with it. The node stands for the generated Go (filer.pb.go, filer_grpc.pb.go, filer_vtproto.pb.go), which is not drawn file by file
weed/pb/filer.proto.what: Declares the SeaweedFiler service: entry lookup (single and batched LookupDirectoryEntries, up to 4096 paths, with per-item read fences, one deduplicated volume location map and exact-fid read tokens), ListEntries (stream; snapshot_ts_ns is a listing time the filer stamps and echoes for event replay, not a store snapshot; omit_chunks), Create/Update/Delete/TouchAccessTime/AppendToEntry, ObjectTransaction(Batch), AtomicRenameEntry and StreamRenameEntry, StreamMutateEntry (one ordered bidirectional stream per mount), PosixLock, volume assignment and lookup, collections, statistics, Ping, GetFilerConfiguration, TraverseBfsMetadata, Subscribe(Local)Metadata, ListMetadataSubscribers, KvGet/KvPut, CacheRemoteObjectToLocalCluster, the distributed lock RPCs (Lock, Unlock, FindLockOwner, TransferLocks, ReplicateLock) and the mount peer registry (MountRegister, MountList). Core types: Entry (chunks, FuseAttributes, extended map, inline content, remote entry, hard link id, quota, worm_enforced_at_ts_ns, commit_ts_ns), FileChunk (fid, offset, size, modified_ts_ns, cipher key, compression, manifest flag, per-chunk SSE type and metadata), EventNotification and SubscribeMetadataResponse (batched events, log file refs for direct reads, flushed watermark, mutation_ts_ns).
